entry.evidence: Adding graph.js (Phase 5 DAG slice) left the Graph view blank with no console error; `window.renderGraphView` was undefined because /graph.js returned 404 — it was referenced in index.html but missing from `_STATIC`.
entry.falsifier: If `_STATIC` is ever replaced by a safe directory-scan static handler, this gotcha disappears.
entry.lesson: The web bridge serves only files explicitly listed in `webserver._STATIC` (an allowlist, not a directory scan). A new webapp asset not added there 404s — and the failure is SILENT: no console error, the missing script just never runs, so its side effects (e.g. a `window.*` render hook) are undefined and the view renders empty. When adding a file under src/portolan/webapp/, add its route to `_STATIC` and restart the server (routes are read at start).

entry.evidence: 2026-07-08 D23 ratified golden_patent.json (25 items); all three properties proven; CI run 28967191374 green.
entry.falsifier: a future need to freeze per-field rather than whole-item (e.g. cosmetic rationale edits shouldn't break the gate) — then hash only the label-bearing fields.
entry.lesson: When a golden/oracle set is ratified, make "the oracle is sacred" mechanical: sha256 the canonical form of ONLY the ratified item ids (`layer_e.ratified_manifest_sha256`), stamp it in a `ratified` block, and add a Layer-0 test that recomputes + compares. Hashing only the frozen ids (not the whole list) is what keeps it APPEND-ONLY — new items may be added freely; frozen ones can't change without a re-stamp. The test must read only the JSON (no corpus store) so it runs in CI (conftest.py auto-marks everything under tests/ as layer0), not just locally. Prove it bites before trusting it: tamper→fail, append→pass, delete→caught.

entry.falsifier: Google changing to distinguish thumb vs full by path/query (then select on that instead of size).
entry.lesson: When scraping patent figures (or any asset that comes in multiple resolutions under one filename), don't take the first URL match — you silently get the 82×120 thumbnail. Google Patents lists each `…-drawings-page-N.png` at TWO storage paths (thumb + full scan); download the candidates and keep the largest by bytes (full-res is 2320×3408). General rule: after fetching image assets, verify resolution (dimensions or byte size), don't trust the URL.

entry.evidence: 2026-07-17 D28 on US5447630A — FIG.6's D1-D6 produced fake numerals 1-6 "located" on page 9; "FIGS. 3 A-C" produced phantom figure 3; both found by cross-checking mapped output against known text-side facts, both test-pinned.
entry.falsifier: a patent corpus where letter-prefixed runs ARE numerals (e.g. part numbers like "A12" used as reference numerals — then scope the rejection per-corpus).
entry.lesson: Two extraction traps when joining patent text to OCR'd drawing sheets: (1) sheets annotate DIMENSIONS as D1/D2/…, and naive digit-run extraction turns them into phantom reference numerals 1/2/… that falsely "match" real text numerals on the wrong sheet — reject digit runs immediately preceded by a letter; (2) captions use spaced letter-ranges ("FIGS. 3 A-C") that a simple FIG-ref regex reads as a phantom bare figure "3", silently occupying an assignment slot (it blocked FIG-4's elimination) — expand letter-ranges explicitly. Same species as the ≥10-floor bug: a plausible extraction rule silently manufacturing or deleting evidence; validate extraction by inspecting BOTH what it keeps and what it discards/creates.

entry.evidence: 2026-07-08 ≥10-floor; 2026-07-17 denial-cue census (L0004); 2026-07-22 OCR no-floor + the consecutive-numeral-check → reconciliation pivot.
entry.falsifier: a corpus where the discarded/flagged items are genuinely what you thought (then the naive check is fine — but you only know by running it on real data first).
entry.lesson: Before shipping any filter/floor/completeness-check on the evidence path, run it on the REAL corpus and inspect BOTH what it keeps and what it flags/discards. Four instances: (1) MIN_NUMERAL≥10 deleted real single-digit reference numerals [deletes signal]; (2) the denial-cue census showed a proposed abstain-gate would fire only false positives [floods FP]; (3) an OCR confidence floor would delete real patent numerals — they carry LEADER LINES that fuse with the digit → conf ~0.3, so low-conf reads ARE the real ones ("89" reads "89-" @0.3) [deletes signal]; (4) a naive "all consecutive reference numbers present?" check produced 85+ false gaps — patents SKIP reference numerals by design, and quantities ("220° F") + OCR misreads corrupt the range [floods FP]. In (4) the reliable check turned out to be a RECONCILIATION (spec-recited vs OCR-drawn disagreements) that never enumerates a contiguous sequence. Precision>>recall governs OUTPUT (never present a wrong answer), NOT input pruning or eager flagging — both erode trust the opposite way.

entry.evidence: 2026-07-22 D28 --confirm on US5447630A recovered 16 spec-predicted numerals the first pass missed incl. the FIG-4 "10" Julian spotted (mismatches 16→9); prototype-first showed tiling recovered 10/52/84/90/95 while lowered-height whole-image recovered none; y-flip bug found + fixed, box verified dead-on in the browser.
entry.falsifier: a corpus where the guiding source is itself unreliable enough that its predictions inject errors into the second pass (then the second look needs its own confidence gate, not blind acceptance of a predicted match).
entry.lesson: When two evidence sources should corroborate but don't (spec text predicts reference numeral N on FIG Y's sheet; first-pass OCR didn't find it there), don't just flag the gap — use the prediction to look again, GUIDED. Concretely for OCR of sparse line-art: whole-image OCR downsamples and drops small isolated numerals, but re-OCR in overlapping full-resolution TILES recovers them; searching ONLY for the text-predicted numeral (not all tile output) is what keeps the higher-recall pass from adding noise (page/patent-number fragments). Two independent sources agreeing is the acceptance bar; a numeral even the guided pass can't confirm STAYS flagged (stronger review signal, not silently filled). Keep it ingestion-time + frozen/hashed so runtime stays deterministic (D28/I6). GOTCHA: a CG sub-image tile rect is TOP-left origin but Vision's boundingBox is BOTTOM-left — the y-axis must be flipped back into the full-image frame (x composes directly), else recovered boxes land mirrored; verify a box lands on the mark.

entry.evidence: 2026-07-22 QA round 2 on US5447630A — 14a via a↔0, 64/88 via 8x4 fallback, fake 1/1/C rejected, B reclassified from whole-image, A honestly flagged; all test-pinned.
entry.falsifier: an engine whose confusion pairs differ (then the variant table is per-engine config, not a constant) or tile OCR with reliable lone-glyph reading (then relax rule 3 with evidence).
entry.lesson: When turning OCR recall UP (tiling, more candidates), three failure modes appear and each has a deterministic counter: (1) CHARACTER CONFUSIONS — Vision reads a trailing 'a' as '0' ("14a"→"140"); recover by matching the confusion variant GATED on the variant not being a known label (reserved set), and record under the true label with the raw read preserved; the reconciliation then resolves positional twins as likely-misreads instead of anomalies. (2) FRAGMENTS — tiles cut tokens ("12b"→"1") and re-read neighbours ("84" emits "4"); reject any hit box-OVERLAPPING (not center-distance — raw reads are wide) a longer token containing it, in existing records, raw observations, AND the fresh hits themselves (longest wins). (3) LONE GLYPHS — single letters hallucinate freely on line art in tiles (a curly leader reads "C!"), but the whole-image pass has layout context: accept single-letter labels ONLY from whole-image observations; a predicted glyph neither pass can read stays FLAGGED (a human saw it → known blind spot), never silently absent.

entry.evidence: 2026-07-22 D29 — the A on US5447630A FIG 2: three engines apparently blind → instrument check → tesseract reads it unguided (edge band, psm 11); the finding shipped as multi-engine complementarity instead of a false "universally unreadable" flag.
entry.falsifier: an environment where /tmp is readable by spawned tools (the corollary is env-specific; the known-positive discipline is not).
entry.lesson: When every engine/tool returns EMPTY on input you can see is valid (a clean "A" glyph three OCR engines "couldn't read"), suspect the harness before the subject: run the same call on a synthetic known-positive. Here tesseract "returning empty" on every crop was a sandbox file-access failure (spawned binaries cannot read /tmp; leptonica's error went to stderr, which the harness decoded but never checked) — a synthetic-A test exposed it in ONE call, and the "blind" engine then read the real glyph at conf 0.96, flipping the entire redundancy conclusion. Corollaries: (1) always surface stderr when a subprocess returns empty stdout; (2) write scratch files to the session scratchpad, not /tmp — the sandbox treats them differently; (3) an "unreadable by everything" conclusion is load-bearing and deserves a positive control before being recorded.

entry.evidence: 2026-07-26 D34 — the OCR failure-mode swarm found the uninstalled L0009 corollary and the zero-consumer `image_sha256`; both closed with `_assert_engine_ran` + `verify_raster_binding` and 4 tests.
entry.falsifier: a lesson whose enforcement genuinely cannot be mechanized (a judgment call about scope or tone) — those stay prose legitimately, but should say so explicitly rather than reading as an unimplemented TODO.
entry.lesson: A lesson written into LIBRARY/CLAUDE.md but not ENFORCED by a check is a lesson the project will pay for twice. L0009's own corollary ("always surface stderr when a subprocess returns empty stdout") sat as prose across four milestones while the code it described — `subprocess.run(..., capture_output=True)` with `returncode` and `stderr` never read — stayed exactly as it was; a research swarm rediscovered it as a live silent-dropout risk, and quantified the blast radius the prose never did (dropping any one engine loses 10-17% of labels, indistinguishable from a clean read). Two structural corollaries. (1) When writing a lesson, ask "what line of code or test would have caught this?" and write THAT in the same change — if the answer is "none", the lesson is an observation, not a mitigation. (2) A hash/field/flag with exactly ONE consumer — the line that WRITES it — is decoration, not a guarantee; `grep` the write site's field name and count readers before claiming it protects anything (`image_sha256` had zero readers while the figures view rested on the raster binding it purported to guard).

entry.evidence: This session — embedding decoded mono audio (first as a binary `var`, then as a base64 string) into the ManifoldObjects state made Ableton stop persisting all Morphos state; a base64 fix did not help (size, not encoding, was the cause); switching to a support-folder copy + path reference restored general saving.

entry.lesson: Do NOT embed large binary (audio samples — megabytes of float or base64) directly in `getStateInformation`'s state chunk. Some hosts (observed: Ableton Live 12 Beta) then silently fail to persist the plugin state ENTIRELY — the session/preset keeps an older or empty chunk, and ALL state stops saving (walls, LFOs, params — not just the sample). entry.evidence: 2026-07-27 — a patch with many high-speed Morphons and several Flux Gates blew up to maximum output with a click and left Ableton's master meter pegged until the session was quit. Ableton's log showed no crash/error (only unrelated July-20 crash reports and July-24 CPU overloads), consistent with float poisoning rather than a fault. Path: friction defaults to 0 → no damping → velocity grows unbounded; fast Morphons sweep pitch zones whose semitone accumulator was explicitly unclamped → `2^(semis/12)` explodes → partial frequencies ≫ Nyquist → an above-Nyquist partial still in the skip list (its previous amp above the floor) keeps advancing its phase by ≫ 1 per sample → phasor escapes [0,1) → out-of-range `kSineTable` reads.
entry.falsifier: If a build with the LUT index masked, the phasor floor-wrapped, partial frequencies clamped below Nyquist, and the output sanitised still produces a stuck full-scale meter, then the explosion originates somewhere other than the additive phasor/LUT path (check the granular read head and the mod-matrix writes next).
entry.lesson: Any table lookup whose index comes from an accumulating phasor must bound the index **inside the lookup**, never by trusting the caller's wrap. Two specific traps that combined here: (1) a phase wrap written as a single `if (p >= 1) p -= 1` only corrects an overshoot < 1, so any per-sample increment > 1.0 leaves the phasor climbing forever; (2) `table[(int)(p * SIZE)]` with an out-of-range `p` reads past the array — arbitrary heap bytes reinterpreted as float samples, i.e. full-scale garbage in the output (and formally UB). Symptom is a **click then a pegged meter that persists until the session is closed**, with NO crash and NO host log entry, because a NaN/Inf sample propagates through the mixer and sticks. Guard at every layer: clamp stored frequencies below Nyquist so increments stay < 1; wrap with `p -= floor(p)`; mask the LUT index (`& (SIZE-1)` when SIZE is a power of two) and map non-finite input to 0; bound any unbounded accumulator (pitch-zone semitones, particle velocity); and sanitise the output buffer for non-finite as a last resort.

entry.evidence: 2026-07-31 — after shipping two wave-terrain click fixes the user still heard clicks and reasonably suspected a cached build. There was no way to tell from inside the plugin, so the fix could be neither confirmed nor ruled out, and the next diagnosis would have been built on an unknown. Adding the stamp made it checkable immediately.
entry.falsifier: If a host is shown to always load the newest binary on rescan (so a stale-cache state is impossible), the stamp is redundant for that host.
entry.lesson: Put `__DATE__ " " __TIME__` (not just a version string) somewhere always visible in the plugin UI — the status bar is ideal. Hosts cache plugin binaries per instance, and a rescan often does NOT pick up a rebuild, so after any install the honest question is "am I hearing my fix or a stale binary?" A version number cannot answer that, because it doesn't change between rebuilds. A compile timestamp does, and it converts an unfalsifiable debugging session into a two-second check. When the stamp is older than the install, remove and re-add the plugin instance — a rescan alone is not reliable.

entry.evidence: 2026-07-31 — user reported crackling "at the low end in particular" after the orbit-closure and buffer-interpolation fixes had already removed the broadband scratch. Numerically sweeping orbit centres across the Manifold showed per-surface DC of 0.08–0.36 with a swing up to 0.73, and a DC that drifts continuously as the centre moves.
entry.falsifier: If low-end crackle persists with the DC blocker engaged and the terrain signal measures DC-free at the output, the cause is elsewhere — check aliasing from Scale×Radius, and voice-sum clipping ahead of the master gain.
entry.lesson: A wave-terrain voice needs a DC blocker; the other engines don't. An additive voice is a sum of sines (mean zero by construction) and a granular voice is windowed (mean ~zero), but a terrain orbit samples whatever patch of surface it happens to sit on, and that patch's MEAN is arbitrary. Measured on the shipped surfaces: DC up to 0.36, swinging 0.73 across the Manifold. That offset is then multiplied by the amplitude envelope (a thump at note-on/off), wanders as the Morphon travels (subsonic drift), and SUMS across voices, eating headroom. Symptom is low-end crackle that worsens with polyphony — not the high-frequency buzz that aliasing or a discontinuity produces. Fix: a one-pole DC blocker (`y = x − x[-1] + R·y[-1]`, R from ~18 Hz) per voice on the terrain signal only, applied BEFORE the envelope so the envelope shapes a DC-free signal. Generalises: any synthesis that reads a position-dependent function (terrain, wavetable scanning, sample scrubbing) can carry position-dependent DC.

entry.evidence: 2026-08-02 — after terrain-specific click fixes (orbit closure, buffer interpolation, DC blocking, level calibration) the user reported clicking on the low end "on additive as well, and possibly granular". Engine-independence ruled out every engine-local cause and pointed at the shared path, where the voice loop did `if (!m.active) { wasActive = false; continue; }` — a hard cut at whatever amplitude the voice held.
entry.falsifier: If low-end clicking persists with fade-out on deactivation, pan and engine gains interpolated, and the polyphony cap high enough that no stealing occurs, the discontinuity is upstream in the physics snapshot (check for amplitude or position jumps between ticks) rather than in the audio path.
entry.lesson: When a synth voice stops while still audible, the discontinuity is a STEP, and a step's spectrum falls off as 1/f — so its energy is concentrated at LOW frequencies. Expect the symptom to be reported as "clicking in the low end", and note it will appear on EVERY engine equally, because the cut happens after the engines are summed. That combination — low-frequency, engine-independent — is the signature that distinguishes it from an engine-specific artefact (aliasing and phase discontinuities are bright and usually engine-local). Normal note-offs don't trigger it, because the envelope reaches zero before the voice is deactivated; the culprits are the paths that deactivate a voice ASYNCHRONOUSLY at whatever amplitude it happens to hold — voice stealing at the polyphony cap, cap-reduction culls, and any "kill on contact" object. Fix: never drop a voice that still has level; render one more buffer ramping its amplitude to zero using its last parameters. Corollary for this architecture: every per-buffer constant that tracks a SPATIAL field (engine mix gains, pan, anchor volume) must be interpolated across the buffer, or it steps at buffer rate — ~94 Hz, also squarely in the low end.

entry.evidence: 2026-08-03 — after the shared voice-cut fix (L0005), additive was fully clean but terrain kept a smaller low-end crackle. The only remaining terrain-unique path was the orbit-centre buffer lerp, which ignored wrap teleports; ratio was also still a per-buffer constant. Both interpolate now.
entry.falsifier: If terrain low-end crackle persists with wrap-aware centre lerp and ratio interpolation, with a STATIC Morphon (no edge crossings) and a single anchor, then the residual is not positional — measure the rendered voice with the offline harness and check the DC blocker transient response next.
entry.lesson: When an engine derives its waveform from a POSITION (wave terrain's orbit centre; future wavetable scan positions), every position interpolation in the audio path must respect the Manifold's topology. On Wrap, a Morphon crossing the edge teleports its coordinate by ~±1; a plain R² lerp from the previous buffer's centre then sweeps the read point across the ENTIRE interior in one buffer — Scale× full surface periods in ~10 ms — a low-frequency burst on every edge crossing. Engines whose position-dependence is already smoothed elsewhere (additive's spectrum lerp, granular's per-grain reads) are immune, so the symptom is engine-specific low-end crackle that survives all shared-path fixes. Fix: shortest-path interpolation on the torus — if |Δ| > 0.5, shift the previous centre by ±1 before lerping; periodic evaluation (sine-table floor-wrap) makes out-of-[0,1] centres read correctly. Residual limits, inherent not bugs: with non-integer Scale the surface itself is seam-discontinuous at the wrap edge (the surface tiles the torus only at integer Scale), and Klein's x-mirror is a genuine seam; the queued boundary-crossing crossfade is the mask for both.

entry.evidence: Three independent surfaces, two observed and one predicted. (1) Parameters.h ID strings — already permanent by rule since Phase 0 precisely because DAW automation keys to them (DECISIONS D006). (2) Mod-matrix srcType/dstType as ints — inserting one destination silently re-pointed every saved connection (D024, the occurrence that produced this lesson). (3) PREDICTED, not yet observed: the mixer's channel strips are derived state that appears and vanishes as samples load, so a level keyed to a strip index would be re-assigned on reload (D033). Flagged as prediction, not a third sighting — it is the reason to build it right, not evidence that it broke. | evidence: 2026-08-04 — FieldObjectCurve was first inserted mid-enum in ModDestType, which would have corrupted every saved mod connection; caught in review, moved to the end, then replaced the whole int scheme with modDestKey / modSourceKey stable strings (load prefers key, falls back to int).
entry.falsifier: A persisted ordinal reference that survives insertion, deletion and reordering of what it points at without a migration. If one exists, the general form is too strong and should retreat to the enum-specific reading. | falsifier: If a patch saved with string keys loads a connection to the wrong destination after an enum reorder, the key path is broken (check the load-order: legacy int first, key overrides) — the scheme, not just the table, is wrong.
entry.lesson: GENERAL FORM — if a thing is saved, automated, or pointed at by another record, it must be identified by something that does not move: a string key, a stable id, a name. Never by an ordinal — enum position, array slot, list index. The failure is always the same shape and always silent: the referent moves, the reference does not follow, and nothing errors. It has now surfaced three times in this codebase wearing three different costumes (see evidence), which is why this was promoted from the enum-specific reading below. SPECIFIC FORM (the original occurrence) — Any enum whose values are written into saved state as ints (mod-matrix srcType/dstType, object type/shape/mode fields) freezes the enum's ORDER into every user session — one mid-enum insertion silently renumbers every saved value and misroutes connections with no error. "Append-only" comments contain the damage but are doctrine-by-vigilance and accumulate as permanent ordering debt. The structural fix: give each enum value a stable string key (like the Parameters.h ID strings — keys are forever, order is free), save the key as authoritative, keep reading the legacy int as fallback for old saves. Put the key table in the same header as the enum, as a switch with NO default case, so -Wswitch makes the compiler flag any new enum value missing a key. Once a release ships and legacy-int loading is retired, the ordering constraint dies entirely.

entry.evidence: 2026-08-04 — the Curve knob shipped dead: the script's add-reset regex asserted AFTER PhysicsState.h was written but BEFORE PhysicsEngine.cpp was, losing exactly two edits (drain case + snapshot copy). The build passed; the drain switch's default swallowed the command; user report "Curve doesn't seem to be doing anything" was the first detection.
entry.falsifier: If a grep-verified full-site wiring pass still yields a dead control, the checklist itself is missing a site — extend the checklist rather than trusting it.
entry.lesson: A multi-site wiring pass (the 14-site object checklist) applied by a script that edits several files in memory and writes at the end can FAIL mid-run (regex/assert miss) and silently discard the edits to any file not yet written — while edits to already-written files survive. The build then passes, because a missing `case` in a switch WITH a default compiles clean and becomes a silent no-op feature: the UI sends the command, physics drops it. Verify wiring by grepping each expected site (count occurrences per file against the checklist) after the pass, never by build success alone; and treat "slider does nothing" as a likely dropped-edit symptom before suspecting the math.

error: invalid supersedes: 'refines L0007-era vortex notes; the saturation described in PR #9 was insufficient, not wrong-direction.'
raw: [L0009] "Zero-work" velocity forces are energy pumps in discrete time — rotate, don't force-add; and decaying drive ≠ bounded drive | tier: candidate | added: 2026-08-05 | tags: physics-geometry, dsp-perf | lesson: Two ways a friction-0 system acquires unbounded energy that look correct on paper: (1) A velocity-perpendicular (magnetic/Lorentz) force is zero-work in continuous time, but integrating it as an explicit force add (v += ω·dt·(ẑ×v)) rotates AND lengthens the velocity by √(1+(ω·dt)²) every tick — an exponential pump proportional to tick rate and ω². Apply it as an EXACT ROTATION of the velocity vector after force integration (Boris-integrator style): conservation by construction, one sincos per Morphon. (2) A drive force that merely DECAYS with speed (e.g. 1/(1+(v/k)²) saturation) never reaches zero work, so with no sink its energy input integrates without bound — speeds grow forever, just slowly. entry.lesson: In a system where modulation is derived from a particle's location, every position-derived parameter co-varies — pan tracks timbre tracks detune — because they are all the same function of the same input. The escape is not more spatial dimensions but the particle's OTHER state: speed, heading, and path curvature depend on how it ARRIVED, so the same point yields different values on different passes. Curvature specifically: κ = |v × a| / |v|³ with a = Δv/dt, i.e. 1/turn-radius. entry.evidence: 2026-08-05 — user reported "walls are acting as emitters". Two live paths: the onset-Stagger gate (added the same week) skipped the prev refresh, and the Terminus arrival snap teleported without the flag. Both fed applyWalls a canvas-spanning segment.
entry.falsifier: If Morphons still appear at walls with prev seeded at spawn, pinned during gates, and every teleport flagged, then the projection is being triggered by a genuine (non-phantom) crossing — check the rail-snap path in applyPathConstraints, which also moves Morphons before applyWalls.
entry.lesson: Collision and crossing detection here works on the segment prev → cur, so the ENTIRE system depends on prev being refreshed every tick and on discontinuous moves being flagged. Two ways to break it, both silent: (1) an early `continue` before the refresh (added for a legitimate reason — gating a delayed voice) leaves prev holding the position of whatever object last occupied that RECYCLED slot, so the phantom segment spans the whole Manifold on every tick of the gate; (2) a teleport (terminus snap, pin, respawn) executed AFTER the refresh without setting the teleport flag. The symptom is spectacular and misleading: a wall "emits" Morphons, because a wall collision doesn't just detect — it PROJECTS the Morphon onto the wall surface and reflects its velocity, so every spuriously-detected crossing relocates a voice to the wall and launches it. Rules: seed prev at spawn; pin prev = cur in any gate that skips the refresh; set the teleport flag in every discontinuous move; and name the flag for what it means (teleported), not for the one caller that first needed it (wrapped).

entry.evidence: Modal layer measured 645× too hot at 110 Hz and 1299× at 55 Hz, sloping 40:1 across 55–880 Hz; the original Layer-0 modal tests all passed because they asserted only "audible" and "decays" at a single f0. Fixed by one operator; peak became 0.73–0.77 across the whole range. A guard clamping sinθ at 0.05 had been masking the true magnitude (would otherwise be ~5000×). Separately measured and NOT patched: re-striking plateaus at 1.1–2.8 within ~2 s, because a damped resonator reaches energy-in = energy-out — the bound was already physical, so no guard was invented (cf. L0012).
entry.falsifier: A modal level gate that sweeps pitch and still lets a real scaling error through; or a case where the closed-form-derived injection produces a pitch-dependent peak. Would also be weakened if a future "wrong character" report turns out to have no level component at all.
entry.lesson: A two-pole modal resonator struck by seeding state (y[0]=0, y[1]=A) has closed form y[n] = A·r^(n−1)·sin(nθ)/sinθ, so the mode PEAK is A/sinθ. Landing a peak of `gain` needs inject = gain·sinθ (MULTIPLY). Dividing — the intuitive "normalise by the sinθ in the impulse response" move — is wrong by sin²θ AND wrong by a pitch-dependent factor. Two durable generalisations: (1) derive the injection from the closed form of the actual initial condition, never from a hand-wave about the impulse response; (2) a gain gate that measures at ONE frequency cannot see a sinθ leak, so any level oracle on a pitched engine must sweep pitch and assert pitch-INDEPENDENCE, not just a bound. Corollary, twice observed now: a gain-structure error presents to the ear as a TONE problem ("blown out", "like a synth through an amp"), because the excess clips downstream and clipping a resonator bank intermodulates its modes — so on a "wrong character" report, measure absolute level before touching the model.

entry.falsifier: a run where index-aligned 1e-6 comparison over the full solved range passes for a genuinely degenerate or GOE 3-manifold spectrum (would mean the solvers now converge identically and this caution is unnecessary).
entry.lesson: When cross-checking C++ (Spectra shift-invert) eigenvalues against the Python (scipy `eigsh`) reference, do NOT compare index-aligned at 1e-6 across the whole requested range for highly degenerate (flat 3-torus: 6/12/24-fold shells) or dense-chaotic (hyperbolic-like/GOE) spectra: the two solvers resolve near-degenerate clusters in different order and can disagree on the count at a near-degeneracy, shifting the tail and producing huge (10–80%) apparent errors even when the operator is identical. Instead: (a) verify the operator/mesh exactly via a construction-level check (plane-wave eigenvectors for lattices; or an exact match of the well-separated LOW modes — the first ~6 align cleanly), and (b) gate the dense bulk as a SET ("each C++ eigenvalue within ~2% of some Python eigenvalue"), not index-aligned.

entry.evidence: `TetManifold::fillViz` published only `u_ + ripple_ + morph_` (identically zero at rest), so the "Hyperbolic-like (4D)" preset drew pixel-identically to the flat 3-torus it is built on; the question "why does the pseudo-hyperbolic manifold look like a 3-torus?" was answered by "it draws as one" (PR #1, renders/viz/). A 6-neighbour Python estimate of the colour magnitude was wrong — real tet-adjacency p95 = 0.31 vs ramp saturation 0.15 (36% pinned) — and the regression test caught it at 60% saturation because it was first written at 8^3 instead of the shipped 12^3.
entry.falsifier: a preset whose baked metric visibly changes the rendered embedding without the viz publishing the base field (i.e. the metric reaches the picture some other way, such as a renderer that solves for an embedding from edge lengths).
entry.lesson: When the metric is intrinsic (edge lengths / conformal factor, never vertex positions), a viz that publishes only the *gesture delta* renders every preset differing solely by its baked metric as the SAME picture — the base field moves no vertex, so the embedding cannot show it and nothing else will. Publish `baked base + gesture`, not just the gesture. Corollary for the display constants: damp the static base separately from the gesture (so existing gesture calibration is untouched), MEASURE the field's real magnitude against the colour ramp's saturation point rather than estimating it, and calibrate at the resolution the preset SHIPS — a graph-Laplacian gets hotter as the grid coarsens, so tuning on a smaller test mesh calibrates against geometry nobody sees.

entry.lesson: A gatekeeping role defined as "resist letting things INTO the shared core" will still happily push the unfrozen core OUT into consumers — the two directions feel like opposites but are the same error, and the inward guard does not catch the outward case. The tell is an efficiency argument: "converging early turns a rewrite into a re-pointing, same total work, lower risk." That reasoning is valid only if the contract is already correct, so it silently assumes the very thing the phased rollout exists to test. Worse, it destroys the evidence: a consumer that shaped itself around your guess can no longer falsify it, and its eventual "fit" is circular. Applies to any provider/consumer split — shared library, platform team, internal API, design system.

entry.evidence: FOUNDATIONS' correspondent manifest listed 3 consumers, hand-written the same day, with the roster assumption explicitly flagged as unverified in DECISIONS #9. A single scan found 11 repos already holding the standby artifact. Nobody had erred — the notice went wider than the manifest and no mechanism existed to notice. Fixed by tools/sweep_correspondents.py, which reports unregistered repos and refuses to register them (DECISIONS #10). Its own first run then false-flagged a registered repo on a case-insensitive filesystem, which is the same class of error one level down: string identity standing in for real identity.
entry.falsifier: A project where the hand-maintained roster stayed accurate over many months of real change without a mechanical check — or a case where auto-registering discovered parties caused no harm and saved real work, which would make the deliberate-registration half of this wrong.
entry.lesson: Any registry of who-we-talk-to that is maintained by writing prose is wrong from the moment the outside world moves, and the failure is silent and confident — an agent reads the file it was told is authoritative and answers from it. The cost is not the staleness; it is that the roster is exactly the input to "who must be told about this change", so a stale roster silently under-sends every subsequent notice. The fix is not diligence but a deterministic sweep that compares the registry against observable reality (a marker file, an API listing, a directory) and REPORTS the delta — and, critically, that must not also auto-reconcile: discovering a party is not the same as registering one, and a scanner that registers what it finds has replaced a deliberate human act with a directory listing.

entry.evidence: FOUNDATIONS.md §3.2 defines a modulation routing as (source, destination, depth, curve, scope) and devotes its whole treatment to making SCOPE a predicate over addressable objects rather than a tree path — while treating SOURCE as an atom. Two consumers independently reported the hole in source, not scope: HYPERSAW (K1..K8 are one rotor's coupled voices, not independent LFOs — "a matrix design that assumes independent sources cannot express this") and Morphos (spatial modulation sources are "continuous fields sampled at a point, not scalar streams", on another thread at another rate, bypassing the matrix entirely). Neither had seen the other's document. DECISIONS #11.
entry.falsifier: A contract where the richly-treated field turned out to be the only one needing richness, and the adjacent atoms held up across three or more independent consumers. Also falsified if the source-model amendment is ruled down and the five-tuple stands as written.
entry.lesson: When a contract defines a relation as a tuple and one element gets a rich, carefully argued treatment, the elements next to it tend to be quietly frozen as atoms — and the visible sophistication of the treated field makes the untreated neighbour harder to see, not easier, because the section reads as thorough. Reviewing "is this general enough?" field by field will miss it; the question that finds it is "which element of this tuple did we never argue about?"

entry.evidence: FOUNDATIONS' CI carried the kit template's `paths-ignore: ["**/*.md","docs/**"]` while its oracle is almost entirely markdown/JSON consistency (INDEX↔LIBRARY, manifest survey answers, correspondent registry, contract version). Every green tick on a docs change had run nothing. Removing the filter (PR #1, 2026-08-10) turned CI red in 6s and exposed two gates broken the whole time: the correspondent sweep failed off the dev machine because it treated absent sibling repos as our data being wrong (a machine detector, not a check), and the standby-notice hash was computed, printed, and compared to no baseline while its own comment claimed it detected un-versioned edits. Both verified fixed against a HOME-redirected CI simulation before pushing (DECISIONS #28).
entry.falsifier: A project where path-filtered CI ran zero times on a whole class of change over many months and no defect reached the branch — or a case where observing a gate fail on purpose cost more than the defects it would have caught. Also falsified if the simulated-environment discipline turns out to produce false confidence, i.e. a simulation that passes where the real runner fails.
entry.lesson: Two failure modes hide behind the same green tick and both survive indefinitely because the signal for "ran and passed" is identical to the signal for "did not run" and to "ran a check that cannot fail". (a) A CI path filter that skips the job entirely — the badge is green, the coverage is zero, and nobody looks because nothing is red. (b) A check whose result is computed and then never compared to anything, which passes on every input including wrong ones. The countermeasure is not more checks but observing each gate FAIL once on purpose, and — for environment-sensitive checks — running the suite in a simulated foreign environment locally rather than discovering machine dependence through a push/wait/read cycle in public.
entry.recurred: 2026-08-10 — and the recurrence sharpened the lesson. A THIRD mode sits beside the two above and is worse than either: CI that runs, FAILS LOUDLY, and is never read. FOUNDATIONS' main was red for nine consecutive runs across two days (2026-08-08 21:03 → 2026-08-10) while the local oracle was green, and the agent asserted "CI passing" in a delivered artifact on the strength of one check made before the breakage. Not indistinguishable-from-passing — simply unobserved. The distinction matters for the countermeasure: filters and dead checks are fixed by testing gates, but an unread signal is fixed only by something that READS it. Concrete mitigation: `./verify ci` queries main's published conclusion (kept out of `fast`, which must stay offline), charter-bound to run at phase gates. Honest limit, recorded: this is reminder-grade, not enforcement — enforcement would mean a network call in the hot path, which is a worse trade.

entry.evidence: FOUNDATIONS registered Catena as a correspondent because FOUNDATIONS.md §8 names it ("Catena — first PM port") and the registration rule was "registered iff the constitution names it". Catena is in fact the first of three engines (then edgewise, then tribos) integrated INTO unified-pm; the constitution named it as what FORCES the phase, never as the counterparty. The project's own ROADMAP had already recorded unified-pm as F3's active correspondent, so two files contradicted each other and nothing caught it — only one of them was machine-checked. Corrected in DECISIONS #12; the rule now requires "named by the constitution AND a deployable consuming across a repo boundary".
entry.falsifier: An ecosystem where per-repo channels stayed correct through several rounds of modules being absorbed into hosts — or a case where a module inside a host genuinely did owe versions independently of that host, which would mean the deployable is not the right unit either and the real unit is finer.
entry.lesson: Repo layout is a snapshot of how work is currently organised; a contract boundary is a claim about who owes whom a version. They coincide often enough to be mistaken for the same thing, and the mistake is invisible because the wrong answer looks tidy — a channel per repo, everything symmetrical. It costs you when several of today's repos are destined to become modules of one deployable: you create channels that can never have a counterparty, exchanges nobody can answer, and a `ball:` field pointing at nobody. The test that separates them is not "does this have its own repo" but "will this owe me a version, or will its host?" Note the trap in the correction too: several modules inside ONE host are close to one observation, not N — agreement among them is weak evidence for a contract's generality because they share the host's conventions.

entry.lesson: When a harness check against ACCEPTANCE numbers fails on a bit-parity-proven port, suspect the measurement protocol, not the port: probe the JS reference under varied protocols (sampling density, settle windows, retrigger state) until the documented numbers reproduce, then encode THAT protocol in the check. Three L0 rows needed this: shimmer min/max only appears under dense sampling (1/s aliases it flat), dissolve's numbers describe only the initial transient, and the free-row values were snapshots of a ~1/√n fluctuation that no protocol reproduces (→ erratum, regime classification per the tolerance line). Never adjust thresholds to pass — reproduce the measurement or surface an erratum.

entry.evidence: three separate Windows CI failures on 2026-07-17/18, each green on macOS first; fixed in commits for renderer_bench (M_PI + -O3), the root CMakeLists (runtime), and trajectory_check (M_PI again).
entry.falsifier: a shared tools-CMake helper or lint hook makes the per-tool checklist redundant.
entry.lesson: CI builds every tool target on windows-latest/MSVC, and each new add_executable repeats the same three traps: (1) no M_PI without _USE_MATH_DEFINES — use a local kPi constant (bit twice in one day: renderer_bench, then trajectory_check); (2) -O3 is not an MSVC flag — guard target_compile_options with if(NOT MSVC); (3) the project links the static MSVC runtime project-wide (CMAKE_MSVC_RUNTIME_LIBRARY at root — clap-wrapper only sets it in its own scope, and mixing /MT with /MD is an LNK2038 wall). Before pushing any new C++ tool: grep it for M_PI, check its flags are guarded, and don't touch runtime settings per-target.

entry.evidence: PR #4 stranding (traces/2026-07-18-gui-polish.md); PR #5/#6 miss; PR #38 stacked-base stranding → rescue cherry-pick (traces/2026-07-19-subosc-rescue-octave.md). And 2026-07-22: ~14 detune-lab commits pushed to PR #70's branch across ~10 turns AFTER #70 had merged — stranded off main until a fresh-branch rescue (PR #72). FOUR occurrences now; the failure is not knowing the rule but not RUNNING the pre-push state check (rule 0) — make it a reflex.
entry.falsifier: a repo setting (auto-merge with required approvals, or reliable stacked-PR retargeting) makes post-file pushes and stacks safe.
entry.lesson: Commits repeatedly miss their merge window: PR #4 merged into a stacked base after the base's own PR had merged (stranding the GUI off main); a layout+ADSR commit pushed to PR #5's branch landed minutes after the human merged it; and PR #38 (stacked with base=#37's branch) merged INTO that already-merged base — GitHub did NOT retarget the child to main after the base merged, so the sub-osc commit never reached main and needed a cherry-pick rescue. The human merges asynchronously and GitHub's stacked-PR retargeting is unreliable. Rules: (0) BEFORE pushing to any branch you did NOT create this turn, run `gh pr view <branch> --json state` and confirm it is OPEN — a merged PR's branch is frozen, and further pushes strand silently (this is the check that was skipped repeatedly); (1) once a PR is filed its branch is frozen — new work starts a NEW branch off main, even for "the same topic"; (2) prefer independent branches off main over stacked PRs; if you must stack, after the BASE merges immediately verify the child's PR retargeted to main AND that its commit is an ancestor of origin/main (git merge-base --is-ancestor / git branch -r --contains) before assuming it landed; (3) stacked PRs state their merge order in the body.

entry.lesson: The shell kept two hand-maintained key chains (applyParam's and readParam's); adding the dynamics params to one but not the other made get_value fall through to 0 — state saved lies, and the "every value round-trips" check PASSED because both instances lied identically. entry.lesson: ADR-036 shipped the claim "Live via the wrapper delivers MPE as note expressions with no further surface" — false on both legs. clap-wrapper's VST3 layer advertises only the note expressions in its _expressionmap, which defaults to PRESSURE-only behind a compile flag (CLAP_SUPPORTS_ALL_NOTE_EXPRESSIONS) that make_clapfirst_plugins never even forwards; and MPE can arrive as rotating member channels + per-channel 0xE0 CLAP_EVENT_MIDI, a type the shell ignored. entry.lesson: MPE bend was "broken" in Ableton Live through THREE rounds of plugin/wrapper code (ADR-036, ADR-038) — the actual cause was Live's per-device "MPE Settings" toggle being OFF, which makes Live send ordinary non-MPE MIDI that no plugin-side code can rescue. Background web/agent research of the host's documented behavior is far cheaper than another code+build+DAW cycle. This is the concrete "gate was elsewhere" branch of [L0006]: static wrapper analysis correctly said "plugin/wrapper is fine, look host-side," and it was right.

entry.evidence: 2026-07-19 — account hit free-tier Actions limit; PRs stuck 'queued' 30+ min on a public repo; frugal ci.yml shipped in the same PR (#53).
entry.falsifier: the account moves to ample/unlimited minutes or self-hosted runners, making the frugality unnecessary.
entry.lesson: A PR-per-change cadence running a full 3-job matrix (Linux + macOS + Windows) on BOTH push and pull_request drained the account's free GitHub Actions minutes mid-month — macOS runners bill at 10x the standard rate, and docs-only PRs (roadmap/traces/prior-art) triggered full builds for nothing. When it happens, everything sits 'queued' indefinitely (an ACCOUNT-wide block; a public repo's per-run minutes are free, so long queues with nothing starting = spending-limit/incident, not runner scarcity — and strictness/step content NEVER affects queueing, only the runs-on label does). Cost-discipline config: (1) paths-ignore ['**.md','docs/**','traces/**'] so docs skip CI; (2) run once per change — pull_request for PRs, push only on main (post-merge net), not both; (3) concurrency group + cancel-in-progress; (4) put the 10x macOS job post-merge-on-main only when the maintainer already builds+validates macOS locally every PR — keep the cheap Linux verify + the can't-do-locally Windows build on PRs. The local ./verify full (9 oracle chains + pluginval 10 + auval + install) is a STRONGER gate than CI; CI's unique value is the Windows build this Mac can't produce.

entry.evidence: ADR-055 / traces/2026-07-20-spectra-adsr.md — spectra_check.cpp:116,137,205 build SpectraCore directly; chose own params 65-68 (defaults 0.004/0.18) over shared 19-22 (0.003/0.16). verify full 8/8 green AND plugin default reference-exact.
entry.falsifier: an oracle is added that drives the full shell param path (host param push → core) at defaults, so a shared-param default divergence WOULD fail a check — then sharing is safe and this caution no longer applies.
entry.lesson: When adding a second engine's version of an existing control (SPECTRA ADSR alongside the SAW ADSR, ADR-055), the tempting reduction is to reuse the shared shell param ids. But the shared shell param carries ONE default (SAW's attack = 0.003 s), while the second engine's reference wants a DIFFERENT one (SPECTRA = 0.004 s). Routing the shared param into the second engine pushes the wrong default in at plugin load — and the parity harness will NOT catch it, because the golden oracle (spectra_check) constructs the core directly (`SpectraCore c(sr); c.setParam(...)`) and renders at the CORE's own SParams default, bypassing the shell entirely. Result: goldens stay green while the shipped plugin's default silently diverges from the reference, with no oracle guarding the gap. Rule: before deciding a new param can SHARE an existing shell id, check whether any oracle actually exercises the shell→core path at that param's default; if the only guard builds the core directly, give the second engine its OWN param with its OWN reference default so both the goldens AND the shipped plugin are reference-exact by construction (ADR-055 chose this; precedent ADR-042 SPECTRA sub-osc ids 52-55). This is the coverage-gap cousin of [L0005] (there: duplicated read chains lie symmetrically and pass value checks; here: the oracle's construction path skips the integration layer where the lie lives) and a concrete instance of the doctrine's "a comfortable green that doesn't test the real path is the dangerous case."

entry.evidence: ADR-065 / traces/2026-07-23-fold-harmonic-law.md — harm-sync failed at rms 9.736e-2; JS-self 1-ULP gave 9.383e-2 growing 5.62e-2→1.147e-1; stable regimes 1.869e-19 and exactly 0; bracket 3.7e-19→4.4e-13→3.5e-07→9.7e-02; anchor retargeted K 0.6→0.9 (ΔR 0.006→0.462 vs 0.2 gate).
entry.falsifier: a regime flagged chaotic by the ULP test later renders sample-exact across independently-compiled implementations, or the divergence is traced to an actual expression difference — then the test produced a false "chaotic" verdict and the diagnosis procedure is unsound.
entry.lesson: When one parity scenario fails by ~5 orders of magnitude while its neighbours pass at rms 0, the established causes are protocol mismatch (L0002) or a genuine port bug — but there is a third: the REGIME ITSELF is chaotic, and no implementation could pass. The decisive test costs one render and involves no C++ at all: perturb the JS reference's initial state by 1 ULP and re-render JS-vs-JS. If that self-divergence matches the C++-vs-JS rms and GROWS over the render (positive Lyapunov exponent), sample-exact parity is impossible in principle — Math.sin and std::sin are not identically rounded, and the dynamics amplify the last bit. Bracket first (divergence should scale with the destabilising params — coupling × spread here) so the ULP test confirms rather than excuses. Resolution is never a loosened ε: remove the golden, cover the regime with a behavioural anchor (bounded, NaN-clean, the qualitative claim the param exists to make, checked with margin), and probe the anchor's own regime — a K where coupling lifts R by 0.006 is chaotic jitter that could flip sign on a legitimate refactor; anchor where the effect is unmistakable. The evidence standard (bracketed curve AND reference-only perturbation, never a bare "just floating point") is now codified in ACCEPTANCE §L0-1's Domain limit clause.

entry.evidence: ADR-065 (reach→harmReach) + ADR-066 (law 3→5) — two collisions in one seven-fold campaign, each caught by grepping swarm_core.h before the edit.
entry.falsifier: lab and core identifiers become single-sourced (generated from one table), making collisions structurally impossible — then the grep discipline is obsolete.
entry.lesson: The audition lab names its params and numbers its menus for its own UI, with no knowledge of the core's members or enum tables — so a literal transcription can collide silently in two ways: (1) NAME collision — the lab's `reach` (harmonic-law top rung) vs the core's existing `reach` (ring-topology radius, ADR-030): a duplicate member with a clashing meaning in the same struct; (2) INDEX collision — the lab's law 3 (stretch) vs the core's law 3 (tempo grid, ADR-022): transcribing the lab's number would have OVERWRITTEN the tempo-grid law, and dyn-grid (which selects law 3 via coreToDyn) would have rendered an inharmonic stack while still called a grid — plausibly staying green. Rule: before folding any lab identifier, grep the destination for the bare name and the enum value; on collision, rename/renumber AT THE FOLD (harmReach; law 5) and record the lab↔core mapping in the ADR and in BOTH law tables, so the next transcription doesn't re-derive it wrong. The lab is an instrument to play, not a naming authority — never renumber the lab to match.

entry.evidence: docs/design/shape-lab.html aliasing block + traces of the 2026-07-27 shape-bench build; broken metric reported plain-saw BLEP -27.7 dB (leakage floor), midpoint sampling reported -149.5 dB and revealed fractional sync as a -62 dB hot spot that the broken metric had hidden.
entry.falsifier: a residue metric that sums all non-signal bins is shown to agree with midpoint sampling on a case where the signal has many strong components — then leakage is not dominating and the simple sum is adequate.
entry.lesson: Building the shape lab's aliasing gate, the obvious metric was "sum every FFT bin that is not within a couple of bins of a harmonic, divide by harmonic energy." It reported a textbook-clean polyBLEP sawtooth at -27.7 dB, which is absurd — a correct polyBLEP saw is around -150 dB. The metric was not measuring aliasing at all: with a dozen strong harmonics below Nyquist, each one's Hann-window skirt contributes a little to thousands of "non-harmonic" bins, and the sum of thousands of tiny leakages dominated the actual fold-down energy. Every comparison built on it would have been noise-vs-noise, and — worse — it would have looked plausible, because the RANKING between configs was still roughly right. The fix is to sample the residue where the signal cannot reach: at the inter-harmonic MIDPOINTS ((k+0.5)*f0), the nearest harmonic is hundreds of bins away and Hann leakage there is below -100 dB, so whatever remains is genuinely alias. Corrected, the same test read -149.5 dB for the clean saw and exposed a real 87 dB spread between configurations that the broken metric had compressed into 15 dB. GENERAL RULE: when measuring a small quantity in the presence of a large one, do not define the small quantity as "total minus large" — find a place in the domain where the large quantity is structurally absent and measure there. Applies to spectral residue, noise floors, crosstalk, and any A-minus-B difference metric where B is orders of magnitude bigger.

The metric was not measuring aliasing at all: with a dozen strong harmonics below Nyquist, each one's Hann-window skirt contributes a little to thousands of "non-harmonic" bins, and the sum of thousands of tiny leakages dominated the actual fold-down energy. Every comparison built on it would have been noise-vs-noise, and — worse — it would have looked plausible, because the RANKING between configs was still roughly right. The fix is to sample the residue where the signal cannot reach: at the inter-harmonic MIDPOINTS ((k+0.5)*f0), the nearest harmonic is hundreds of bins away and Hann leakage there is below -100 dB, so whatever remains is genuinely alias. Corrected, the same test read -149.5 dB for the clean saw and exposed a real 87 dB spread between configurations that the broken metric had compressed into 15 dB. entry.evidence: 2026-07-28 session — server on 127.0.0.1:8173 verified as the sole listener and serving the correct file, rendered correctly in the browser pane, unreachable for the human; `curl /.git/config` returned 200 at repo root and 404 after scoping; resolved by `open docs/design/shape-lab.html` with no server.
entry.falsifier: a sandboxed Bash-started server is shown to be reachable from the host browser on this setup — then the sandbox does not isolate loopback and only the directory-scoping half of this lesson stands.
entry.lesson: Serving a lab over `python3 -m http.server` worked perfectly in the in-app browser pane and was completely unreachable for the human, who reasonably concluded the port was already occupied. It was not: the bind succeeded and was the only listener on that port. The cause is that Bash tool calls run inside a sandbox, so a socket bound to 127.0.0.1 there is on a different loopback than the host's browser sees. The in-app pane shares the agent's environment and therefore cannot detect the problem. Two consequences: (1) DO NOT use the in-app pane rendering a page as evidence that the human can see it — those are different networks; (2) for a self-contained HTML artifact (all script/style inline, no fetch, no modules) there is no reason to run a server at all — `open <file>` in the host browser is simpler, has no port to collide, and works first time. If a server genuinely is needed (module imports, fetch, CORS), start it with the sandbox disabled so it lands on the host loopback. SECOND, INDEPENDENT TRAP found the same round: a quick `http.server` at the repo root serves `.git/` and every source file over HTTP. Localhost-only bind limits the blast radius but does not make it acceptable — scope the server to the directory being shown (`--directory docs/design`) as a matter of course.

entry.evidence: 2026-07-28 shape-lab session, all three instances measured and corrected: aliasing -27.7 -> -149.5 dB after inter-harmonic midpoint sampling (and it then revealed an 87 dB spread the broken metric had compressed to 15 dB, incl. the fractional-sync hot spot it hid entirely); formant locator replaced with a 1/3-octave envelope peak; click detector replaced with 2nd-difference outliers vs the robust local median, which then correctly read 0/s on integer sync and 300/s on ratio 4.37.
entry.falsifier: a detector that passes the clean/defective calibration pair is later shown to be measuring the wrong quantity anyway — then calibration is insufficient and a stronger validation (e.g. an independently-derived reference implementation) is required.
entry.lesson: THREE TIMES IN ONE SESSION I built a measurement instrument, got numbers that looked reasonable, and was measuring the wrong thing entirely. (1) An aliasing metric summed every non-harmonic FFT bin — it was accumulating Hann-window leakage from a dozen strong harmonics across thousands of bins, and reported a textbook-clean polyBLEP sawtooth at -27.7 dB instead of -149.5 dB. (2) A formant locator detrended the spectrum by +20log10(k) to cancel the saw's rolloff — that tilt over-weights the top octaves so hard it finds noise, and it reported 3190 Hz for an 800 Hz target. (3) A click detector thresholded |x[n]-x[n-1]| — on a 1200 Hz sine that is just the slope (~0.17/sample at 44.1 kHz), so it reported 2700 "jumps" in a perfectly clean signal, and I nearly chased a bug that did not exist. THE COMMON SHAPE: a threshold on the WRONG DERIVATIVE (or the wrong domain) measures the signal itself rather than the defect. WHY IT SURVIVES SCRUTINY: in all three cases the RANKING between configurations stayed roughly correct, so A/B comparisons still "worked" and nothing looked broken; only the absolute value was absurd. What saved me each time was noticing the absolute number was implausible against a reference I happened to know (a clean polyBLEP saw is ~-150 dB, not -27). That is luck, and it fails silently whenever I do NOT already know the right answer. THE RULE, which is cheap because both cases almost always already exist: before trusting a new detector, run it on (a) a signal known to be CLEAN — it MUST report ~zero, and if it does not, it is measuring the signal; and (b) a signal known to be DEFECTIVE — it MUST report large. Only then interpret real results. Corollary: plausible rankings are NOT validation. Domain-general — applies to any residue, noise floor, crosstalk, error rate, or A-minus-B metric where B is orders of magnitude larger than A. [[L0014]] is the spectral-specific technique that falls out of this (sample where the signal structurally ISN'T); this entry is the general procedure.

entry.evidence: 2026-07-29 reverb stereo work. A sparse probe-frequency (Goertzel sweep) HF/LF metric was calibrated on the reverb tail and read exactly 0.00 dB on two independent mono configurations — genuinely valid there, because the tail is broadband. Reused unchanged on the DRY saw swarm it reported 4.62 dB of tilt at n=7 and -10.76 dB at n=8; the probe grid was landing on harmonics of one detuned voice and missing another's. Rebuilt as a Welch-averaged FFT integrating every bin per band (identical L/R -> 0.000 dB; known 6 dB HF lift -> +9.79 dB), the true worst was 0.65 dB across n=2..12. I had already written and measured a "fix" for the phantom defect before catching it. | RECURRED TWICE 2026-08-03 (promoted candidate->canonical on independent recurrence): building a click detector for the FX comb, I twice compared the wrong classes. First the floor was a DRY SINE (0.0078/sample slope) against a RINGING COMB, whose resonances legitimately exceed it — the bound was meaningless and the correct fix 'failed' it. Then two different NOTE PATTERNS, which differ in line count and entry time, so it measured their configurations rather than the click. Both were fixed by pairing WITHIN one run — worst jump near a note-on vs far from one, same signal, only position differs — which separated 1.01 (fixed) from 16.96 (planted bad). Three occurrences now, in three different domains.
entry.falsifier: a detector that stays accurate across signal classes without recalibration — e.g. one whose calibration cases already span the classes it will meet. The rule is about untested transfer, not about detectors being fragile.
entry.lesson: L0016 says calibrate a new defect metric before trusting it. The unstated half: a calibration certifies the detector FOR THE SIGNAL CLASS IT WAS CALIBRATED ON. Carrying a validated detector to a different class silently re-opens the hole. Re-run the known-clean and known-bad cases every time the signal under test changes character (broadband -> harmonic, steady -> transient, mono -> stereo).

entry.evidence: 2026-07-29 HYPERSAW ensemble lab. The two-slope phase warp behind "spectral smear" measured bit-identical harmonic levels at warpD +1 and -1 (h1..h16 diffs equal to 0.1 dB across the board). Combined with the warp being a monotone 2.73 dB rms TILT rather than a resonant peak, this explained three independent human reports of total inaudibility, and the axis was retired rather than tuned.
entry.falsifier: a phase-warp family whose +d and -d magnitude spectra measurably differ — which requires the map at -d NOT to be the time reversal of the map at +d (e.g. an asymmetric or non-monotone map). The rule is about time-reversal-paired maps, not about all bipolar controls.
entry.lesson: For any waveshaping expressed as a monotone phase MAP, the map at +d and the map at -d are time reversals of each other, and a magnitude spectrum is invariant under time reversal — only the phase flips. So a bipolar warp control has a one-sided magnitude response, and any per-voice DISPERSION symmetric about zero folds onto |d|: half the intended spread lands on top of the other half and voices meant to differ are identical. Check the sign symmetry of any new bipolar spectral axis BEFORE building a dispersion on top of it.

entry.evidence: Wing, Endo, Bradbury & Vorberg (2014), string-quartet timing. At MATCHED variance, asynchrony detection threshold moved 64.3 -> 18.2 ms^2 purely as a function of serial structure; lag-1 autocorrelation 0.84 vs 0.39, p<0.0005 — i.e. structure dominated variance for the perceptual judgement. Surfaced in HYPERSAW's 2026-07-28 orchestral-ensemble research pass (104 agents, 3-vote adversarial verification) and implemented as `EnsembleTiming` in docs/design/ensemble-lab.html. Independent corroboration of the mechanism from the other direction: a Kuramoto phase coupling K is formally the same error-correction gain, so a coupled-oscillator architecture generates this timing natively rather than needing a bolted-on humaniser — the strongest architecture/evidence match the project has found. Recorded as canonical on human review (2026-07-29) rather than on a second occurrence.
entry.falsifier: a listening test in which matched-variance onset jitter with human-like lag-1 autocorrelation and with zero autocorrelation are indistinguishable; or a humanize implementation whose perceived musicality tracks jitter magnitude alone with serial structure held irrelevant. Note the claim is about PERCEIVED ensemble togetherness — it does not assert that variance is inaudible, only that structure dominates it.
entry.lesson: Listeners judge ensemble togetherness from the SERIAL STRUCTURE of onset asynchrony, not from its variance. Independent per-note random offsets — what essentially every "humanize", "groove", or "feel" control does — produce the right variance with the WRONG autocorrelation, and read as sloppy rather than human. Model mutual error correction instead: each part nudges its offset toward the group's mean offset and then adds fresh motor noise, `off_i <- off_i - alpha*(off_i - mean_off) + noise_i`. The human-like lag-1 autocorrelation is then EMERGENT, not dialled in. Two design consequences worth more than the formula: (1) the musically meaningful control is alpha (the correction gain — how hard players pull toward each other, i.e. "tightness"), not the noise amount, which is why humanize knobs calibrated in milliseconds feel wrong at every setting; (2) alpha = 0 is an independent random walk that DRIFTS without bound, and alpha = 1 is rigid quantisation, so the usable musical range is strictly interior — a humanize feature with no correction term has no tightness axis at all, only a sloppiness axis. Applies to any onset-timing humanisation on MIDI or audio: DAW humanize, sequencer swing/feel, drum machines, sample libraries, unison/ensemble patches, multi-agent performance timing.

entry.evidence: 2026-07-30/31 HYPERSAW, THREE distinct staleness incidents in two days, each costing a full debugging round: (1) merged CLAP params invisible in the DAW — the merge changed source, the loaded binary was the old install; (2) "the tool is appearing cached again" — the human's working tree was on a branch cut BEFORE the relevant merge, so their file genuinely lacked the feature I was describing; (3) reverb-lab edits invisible — genuine browser cache of a file:// page. Fixes that ended it: labs gained a git-derived `rev` timestamp PLUS a load-time content fingerprint (hash of the page's own inline scripts — maintenance-free, cannot be stale); the plugin gained a CMake-injected git short hash with a dirty-tree "+" displayed in the GUI corner. Before the stamps, every occurrence required me to run `strings`/`ls -l`/log inspection to answer a question the human should have answered in one glance.
entry.falsifier: an artifact whose runtime provably cannot cache (no install step, no separate process, content re-read on every evaluation) — there, a stamp is noise. Also falsified if a project's staleness incidents are traced to something a stamp cannot expose (e.g. a correct binary loading stale STATE); the rule is about identity of the ARTIFACT, and state provenance is a separate problem.
entry.lesson: Any artifact a human evaluates through a SEPARATE RUNTIME — a plugin loaded by a DAW, a page served to a browser, an app installed to a system path, a container pulled by an orchestrator, a model served behind an endpoint — sits behind at least one cache the human cannot see. When behaviour does not match the source, "is it stale?" must be answerable BY LOOKING AT THE ARTIFACT, not by forensics. Stamp the build identity INTO the artifact, derived from the VCS at build time (never hand-typed: a hand-maintained version lies exactly when it matters, because the moment you forget to bump it is the moment you are debugging), mark a dirty working tree distinctly (e.g. a trailing "+") so an uncommitted local edit can never masquerade as the committed hash, and DISPLAY it where the human already looks. For self-contained artifacts with no build step, compute a fingerprint AT LOAD from the artifact's own content — it cannot go stale by construction, because it describes the bytes actually loaded rather than what someone remembered to type. Corollary: also stamp the SOURCE-of-truth question — when the human is looking at one copy while you describe another (a branch checked out before a merge; a doc regenerated from newer data), the cheap fix is a visible identity, not more explaining.

entry.evidence: HYPERSAW ADR-025 super-width (width > 1, C++-only M/S boost, no JS reference). Its negative cross-feed (L' = 1.5L − 0.5R at width 1.5) injected phase-inverted saws whose wraps are vertical up-cliffs — scoped repeatedly by the human, denied repeatedly by me because every check I ran was structurally blind: JS renders width-clamp by construction; parity goldens and waveshape_check all ran width <= 1. Dose-response once probed in C++: 0 cliffs at width <= 1.01, 1414 at width 1.5. The human isolated it by settings-bisection ("happens when width is turned up above 1") and had named the mechanism days earlier ("a phase-inverted saw mixed in there").
entry.falsifier: a superset region whose behavior is fully constrained by an existing non-parity oracle (e.g. a trajectory or invariant check that genuinely exercises it) — the rule is about UNCOVERED supersets, not about supersets being inherently untestable.
entry.lesson: The reference-parity pattern (C++ must match a frozen reference bit-exactly) only covers the parameter region the REFERENCE implements. A deliberate superset ("C++-only feature, reference range bit-untouched") is invisible to that oracle BY CONSTRUCTION: parity keeps passing forever while the superset region does anything at all. Corollary of L0011 (oracle sees only the path it exercises), sharper form: when a feature is ADDED as a superset, the same commit must add an invariant oracle for the superset region — parity green plus superset-untested is a coverage hole that LOOKS like full coverage.

entry.evidence: HYPERSAW 2026-08-03. Stuck notes survived four rounds of fixes (deferral, emit-on-release, tag retirement, envelope investigation). The core was proven innocent by measurement (post-release tail 46.4 ms at every K setting and both rtone extremes). The actual bug: emitNoteEnds ignored `out->try_push`'s return and retired the note tag regardless; the host's output buffer is finite and drainQueue floods it with param events on every knob move, so sweeping a control could crowd out a NOTE_END, which was then destroyed forever and the host withheld retriggering that pitch. The human's clue — "stalls most when I've recently changed the K value" — was what localised it, since knob movement is exactly what fills the buffer. endprobe now refuses 40 pushes; measured old code 0 ENDs delivered, fixed code 1.
entry.falsifier: an API whose documented contract guarantees acceptance (an unbounded queue, or a blocking write) — there the flag is informational and may be ignored. The rule binds wherever the channel is finite or the call is documented as best-effort.
entry.lesson: When an API hands back a success flag (try_push, try_send, non-blocking write, ring-buffer enqueue), it is telling you the call CAN fail under load. Ignoring the flag and retiring the local state anyway converts a transient, fully recoverable condition into PERMANENT silent data loss. The failure is near-invisible: the rejecting path only triggers when the channel is busy, so it presents as rare, load-correlated flakiness rather than a reproducible bug, and every low-load test passes. Rule: retire local state only on ACCEPTANCE; keep the item queued and retry next cycle. Corollary for the test: a rejecting stub belongs in the harness — and must be proven to FAIL against the pre-fix code, or it proves nothing.

entry.evidence: HYPERSAW ADR-071 widened FX slot types 0..3 -> 0..5 to add Comp and Comb; the four GUI dropdowns in gui.html were never widened with them. Both effects shipped, ran, and were host-automatable while being unselectable in the plugin's own panel — for two weeks, with all ten oracle chains green and parity 147/147. Found only because the human MISremembered the comb as lab-only and I checked the claim instead of accepting it. The follow-on fold (comb resonance, ADR-080) therefore shipped with waveshape_check T7 measuring ring time 99/190/772 ms across the knob's range, specifically to prove the new control reaches the DSP.
entry.falsifier: a codebase where the control surface is GENERATED from the param definitions, so the two cannot disagree — which is the real fix, and makes the lesson an argument for that generation rather than for vigilance.
entry.lesson: when a feature adds values to an existing parameter's range, the change is split across two files — the param definition and the control that offers the choices. Widen only the first and the feature is fully implemented, fully tested, automatable by a host, and absent from the product. Every audio/behavioural oracle passes, because the audio path IS correct; the defect lives entirely in what the user can reach. Treat "widen a range" as an atomic edit spanning param + control, the same way an INDEX pointer must land with its LIBRARY entry. Corollary: an inert-by-default parameter needs a gate proving the knob is CONNECTED, since parity staying green proves only that the default changes nothing.

entry.evidence: HYPERSAW comb declick, 2026-08-03. The second detector version read 1.56x against a 1.6x bound and was GREEN. Rather than ship, I re-derived it: the two runs being compared had different line counts and entry times, so the number was mostly configuration difference. Re-pairing the comparison within a single run (near a note-on vs far from one) gave 1.01 for the fix and 16.96 for the planted-bad — a 17x separation where the marginal detector had shown 1.56x. The fix had been essentially perfect the whole time; only the measurement was marginal.
entry.falsifier: a domain where effect sizes genuinely cluster near the acceptance threshold (incremental performance tuning, statistical A/B at low power), where marginal readings are the norm and this heuristic would cause endless re-derivation.
entry.lesson: a real fix and a real defect usually differ by a lot, because they differ in KIND. When a metric reads just inside its bound, the likeliest explanation is not "the fix barely worked" but "this measurement is dominated by something other than the effect" — a confound, a mismatched baseline, the wrong window. Treat a marginal pass as a prompt to re-derive the measurement, never as permission to ship. The comfortable reading (it passed) is exactly the one to distrust.

entry.falsifier: a project small enough that the narrative IS the index, or one whose tooling derives status from machine-readable state (issue tracker, checkboxes parsed by CI) so the prose cannot drift from it.
entry.lesson: append-only design documents are excellent at preserving reasoning and structurally bad at reporting current state, because an item's status lives inside the paragraph that created it and is never revisited when the world changes. entry.evidence: HYPERSAW 2026-08-06/07 — ADR-082 Amendment 1 (stride full on day one, amendable only pre-exposure); the 13-param misclassification audit (ROADMAP § Re-order, human-directed reorder to mixer-first); preset tier landing "nearly free" from the id scheme (PR #217/#219); K-vs-link distinction (PR #222).
entry.falsifier: a project that builds sources first and retrofits the audio context WITHOUT either breaking saved sessions or freezing wrong boundaries permanently — or one where the mixer-first order itself caused comparable rework (e.g. a channel-strip abstraction that the eventual sources could not fill).
entry.lesson: for an ambitious instrument (multiple oscillators/engines, a morph system, preset tiers, an FX rack), build the AUDIO CONTEXT — the mixer/master page and the routing topology — before doing major work on the sound sources themselves, and settle every cross-cutting axis the same way. The boundary between "belongs to one source" and "belongs to the patch" cannot be decided correctly in the abstract: this project classified 31 params as global by reasoning in an ADR and got 13 wrong (width, mono, inertia, the amp envelope, glide — each oscillator's copy existed but was unreachable), an error the mixer page would have made impossible because a channel strip DECIDES what is per-source. The same sequencing applies to: (1) the param-id namespace (append-only; capacity IS the stride — this project shipped a scheme whose osc-0 block was full on day one and could amend it only because no host had seen the ids); (2) preset tiers (the per-source tier fell out of the id scheme's key prefixes almost free — a format designed before the namespace would have fought it); (3) cross-source coupling semantics (a "master K" that shares a parameter vs a `link` that shares dynamics are different features; naming them requires knowing the routing); (4) global macros (a time-scale macro needs every time-domain param flagged AT INTRODUCTION — auditing later took a scan plus hand-filtering); (5) provenance/ownership display (corner colouring needs a single vocabulary defined before three UIs each invent one). The general form: any axis that CROSSES sources — audio, ids, presets, coupling, macros, display vocabulary — is cheap to define before the second source exists and expensive-to-impossible after, because the first shipped build freezes it.
