entry.evidence: HYPERSAW 2026-08-07/09 — PR #227 (publishViz + XY hardwiring), PR #239 (the unregistered hzSetVizOsc bind, found only when the human reported the viz "still tacked to osc 1"), and the human's framing: visuals should never tack to a specific object but to "a category open to be negotiated via plumbing".  PROMOTED candidate -> canonical 2026-08-09, same day, by a second INDEPENDENT occurrence in an unrelated subsystem: voice lifecycle, not visuals. Eight sites in the CLAP event loop addressed `core` (an alias for oscillator 0) where the intent was "every oscillator" — PRESSURE fanned out but TUNING did not (a bend split the oscillator pair mid-gesture), and every allOff() path (mono/poly toggle, engine switch, MIDI all-notes-off, reset, GUI panic) silenced only oscillator 0, which IS a stuck note. Two things generalise beyond the original entry. (4) THE ALIAS IS THE HAZARD: `SwarmCore &core = cores[0]` existed so the multi-instance port would not have to touch every legacy call site, and that convenience is precisely what made eight wrong sites read as correct code — a compatibility alias over a newly-multiplied resource converts "unported" from a compile error into a silent runtime bug, so it should be introduced only with a deadline to remove it. (5) PARTIAL FAN-OUT IS THE TELL: when one operation of a family fans out and its sibling does not, the port was done by call site instead of by family; grep the whole family the moment you find one.
entry.falsifier: a multi-instance system where per-consumer instance binding stayed correct without a shared indirection — or one where role indirection itself caused comparable harm (e.g. a consumer that genuinely needed a pinned instance, such as an A/B comparison view, forced through a single global role handle).
entry.lesson: every consumer of engine state — visuals, meters, labels, preset scopes, mod destinations — must name a ROLE ("the oscillator being edited", "the master bus", "the focused voice") and resolve it through a documented indirection ON EVERY READ. Binding a consumer to a concrete instance at wire time is invisible while there is only one instance and silently wrong the moment there are two, because the wrong answer is a PLAUSIBLE one: the display keeps working, it just describes the wrong object. Three incidents in one week, same shape: (a) publishViz built every per-swarm visual from `core` — oscillator 0 — so the phase circle described osc 1 no matter which tab was active; (b) the XY pad sent raw base param ids (4/6) rather than effective ids, so both axes wrote oscillator 0 while the panel repainted over the evidence, producing an asymmetric "detune works, K doesn't" illusion; (c) once the indirection existed it was inert for two PRs because its webview binding was never registered — a callback with no bind is invisible to the compiler, so the feature shipped dead and green. Three corollaries: (1) the indirection must be ONE named thing (an index, a handle) that every consumer reads, not per-consumer plumbing — the second copy diverges; (2) THE LABEL IS PART OF THE MECHANISM: a role-addressed display must render which instance it resolved to, because otherwise a mis-resolution is unobservable by eye and the bug survives every "looks fine" inspection — in this project the missing label is precisely why (a) and (c) each survived a merge; (3) identical defaults make role errors invisible, so a role-addressed view needs at least one instance-distinguishing datum on screen (level, name, index).

entry.evidence: HYPERSAW 2026-08-09 — eight sites in the CLAP event loop addressed oscillator 0 where the intent was every oscillator (PR #242): bend split the oscillator pair mid-gesture, and every allOff() path left the other oscillators gated, which is a stuck note. entry.falsifier: an instrument where per-consumer gesture wiring stayed correct across a genuine multiplication of consumers without a routing layer — or one where forcing gestures through the mod matrix cost required immediacy (a per-note tuning that MUST bypass smoothing/depth to stay sample-accurate would be a real counter-pressure, and would argue for a routed FAST LANE rather than for hand-wiring).
entry.lesson: every performance gesture — velocity, aftertouch/pressure, per-note tuning, channel bend, mod wheel — is a SOURCE and must enter the instrument through the same routing layer as every other source, then be distributed to consumers by that layer. HYPERSAW instead grew TWO parallel paths for the same class of signal: a modulation matrix (sources, destinations, depths) AND a hand-wired MPE path in the event loop that reaches consumers directly. The cost is combinatorial and silent: with E event types and C consumers, hand-wiring is E x C independent chances to miss a connection, and every new consumer re-opens all E. That is exactly how PRESSURE came to fan out to every oscillator while TUNING did not — one row of the matrix was filled in and its neighbour was not, and both compiled. Three consequences worth carrying: (1) the fix is NOT a fan-out helper per operation family (that reduces E x C to E and still scales with event types — HYPERSAW's 2026-08-09 patch, honest but not the cure); it is ONE table where a gesture is routed once and every consumer reads the same routing; (2) a routing layer makes the question "does pressure reach oscillator 2?" UNASKABLE, which is stronger than making it answerable — there is no per-consumer wiring to get wrong; (3) the layer must exist BEFORE the second consumer, because the hand-wired path is cheapest exactly while there is one consumer and is never cheap again (L0027's sequencing lesson, instantiated).

The cost is combinatorial and silent: with E event types and C consumers, hand-wiring is E x C independent chances to miss a connection, and every new consumer re-opens all E. That is exactly how PRESSURE came to fan out to every oscillator while TUNING did not — one row of the matrix was filled in and its neighbour was not, and both compiled. Three consequences worth carrying: (1) the fix is NOT a fan-out helper per operation family (that reduces E x C to E and still scales with event types — HYPERSAW's 2026-08-09 patch, honest but not the cure); it is ONE table where a gesture is routed once and every consumer reads the same routing; (2) a routing layer makes the question "does pressure reach oscillator 2?" UNASKABLE, which is stronger than making it answerable — there is no per-consumer wiring to get wrong; (3) the layer must exist BEFORE the second consumer, because the hand-wired path is cheapest exactly while there is one consumer and is never cheap again (L0027's sequencing lesson, instantiated). | evidence: HYPERSAW 2026-08-09 — eight sites in the CLAP event loop addressed oscillator 0 where the intent was every oscillator (PR #242): bend split the oscillator pair mid-gesture, and every allOff() path left the other oscillators gated, which is a stuck note. Human's framing: "MPE should go to the plumbing and get routed from there instead of messy redundancies and missed connections." | falsifier: an instrument where per-consumer gesture wiring stayed correct across a genuine multiplication of consumers without a routing layer — or one where forcing gestures through the mod matrix cost required immediacy (a per-note tuning that MUST bypass smoothing/depth to stay sample-accurate would be a real counter-pressure, and would argue for a routed FAST LANE rather than for hand-wiring).

entry.evidence: HYPERSAW 2026-08-09 — human, on the MPE routing lesson: "This would be a good candidate for having the library build up from scratch efficiently and then we can test against the oracle." mpe_check drives factory -> activate -> events -> process and detects via Goertzel on the output, deliberately not via a state read (the state_check trap, where a round-trip through one broken accessor agreed with itself).
entry.falsifier: a donated oracle that turned out to encode the donor's implementation rather than the requirement — i.e. a correct-but-different implementation fails it. That is the test of whether it was really an oracle; if it happens, the oracle was over-specified and must be loosened to observable behaviour.
entry.lesson: when a mature project seeds a shared library, the instinct is to donate CODE (modules, headers) or RULINGS (docs). The higher-leverage artifact is the ORACLE: an executable statement of required behaviour that names no internals. A donated module carries the donor's accidents — its allocation habits, its aliases, its scope assumptions — and the library inherits them; a donated oracle carries only the requirement, so the library can build the subsystem from scratch, the way it should have been built, and still be held to behaviour that was paid for in real bugs. HYPERSAW's mpe_check is the worked example: it drives the public plugin interface and measures emitted audio, so it names no oscillator, no core, no alias — it would pass or fail an implementation sharing none of HYPERSAW's code. Corollary: this is only true of oracles written against the PUBLIC surface and observable output. An oracle that reads internal state (a per-voice getter) is a code donation wearing a test's clothes, and it pins the recipient's architecture to the donor's.
entry.title: An ORACLE is the most portable thing a project can donate — it transfers the requirement without the implementation

entry.lesson: a ring at temperature 0 with no profile edit MUST reproduce the exact Euclidean pattern E(k,n,rot), regardless of graph, homeostat, seed, or neighbors. entry.evidence: LATHE L2 port-pin, first run failed on the first HAT velocity — golden bits 3fe6e31e66313234 vs port ...3233; adding -ffp-contract=off turned 3 seeds / 3,885 events bit-exact. Lathe DECISIONS #19.
entry.falsifier: a port whose reference itself uses FMA (e.g. C→C with fma() calls), where contraction ON is the faithful setting — the rule is "match the reference's rounding", not "always off".
entry.lesson: porting numeric code to C++ under a bit-exactness pin, the FIRST failure is likely to be ~1 ULP from fused multiply-add: Clang/GCC contract `a*b + c` into one FMA (rounding once, not twice), while the reference language (JavaScript, and most interpreters) has no FMA. Compile the pinned translation unit with `-ffp-contract=off` and comment the flag as load-bearing — it looks like a tuning knob and will be "cleaned up" otherwise. Expression ORDER matters for the same reason: `(1-s)*k/n` ≠ `(1-s)*(k/n)`, and edge-contribution summation order is observable, so mirror the reference's parse tree rather than its intent.
entry.title: A bit-exact numeric port must disable FP contraction before it can pass

entry.falsifier: a reference that cannot be executed headlessly at all (hardware-bound, or hopelessly entangled with UI) — then a transcription plus an independent review of it is the fallback, and its weaker guarantee should be stated.
entry.lesson: when a prototype is the frozen behavioral oracle, produce its golden traces by slicing the reference's own source verbatim and executing it under a thin shim, driven by a committed script that fails loudly if its extraction markers stop matching. Hand-transcribing the reference into the golden generator makes the goldens agree with your READING of the reference rather than the reference itself — which is precisely the error the port-pin exists to catch, and it fails silently because both sides then share the misreading. Corollary: emit exact bit patterns (IEEE-754 hex), not decimals, so the comparison cannot be loosened by formatting.

entry.evidence: LATHE-SPEC §4 claims full permutation invariance; measured, it holds with ornaments off but fails with them on, because one shared RNG stream is consumed in ring-iteration order and ghost fires feed back through fireHist/act. Both directions are now tests; Lathe DECISIONS #18.
entry.falsifier: the system moves to per-ring RNG streams (Lathe open DECISION #6), after which full invariance becomes true and the counter-case test SHOULD fail — deliberately, as the signal that semantics changed.
entry.lesson: when a spec states an invariant broadly ("evaluation order is irrelevant") and testing shows it holds only on part of the system, do not quietly narrow the test to the passing subset — assert the invariant where it genuinely holds AND assert the violation where it does not. The counter-case test is what stops a later change from silently flipping the behavior: it converts an undocumented quirk into a guarded decision. Record the narrowing against the spec rather than editing a protected spec file.

entry.evidence: LATHE-SPEC §4 (synchronous discipline), §5 (cycle policy: warn never block; W1/W2/W3), §6 (homeostat).
entry.falsifier: a coupling design that genuinely needs same-tick (combinational) edges for musical reasons — that reintroduces algebraic loops and would need a different (ordered/iterated-to-fixpoint) evaluation model, breaking the order-independence this rests on.
entry.lesson: because every inter-ring edge reads the source's PREVIOUS-tick state (synchronous snapshot, implicit unit delay), a directed cycle in the dependency graph is a well-defined discrete-time feedback system — exactly the interesting coupling, not a bug. So the engine NEVER refuses to create an edge; a static analyzer attaches warnings (W1 runaway / W2 deadlock / W3 advisory) and runtime guards (homeostat bounds runaway, a liveness watchdog surfaces starvation) keep even ignored warnings safe. Blocking cycles would forbid the feature. This also makes evaluation ORDER irrelevant (permutation test), which is what keeps the whole thing deterministic.

entry.evidence: isonoise retuned from λ∈[16,64] to [6,16] across commits e9f2dac→4d8025c; at the new band measured bicubic ≤0.4% vs bilinear 4–5% centroid error; the D1 oracle lives in `test/oracle/layer0.test.ts` ("resampler rotation invariance").
entry.falsifier: the D1 rotation-invariance oracle still passes after the sampler is swapped to bilinear.
entry.lesson: A resampler rotation-invariance fixture (the isonoise DEM) must carry energy near the raster Nyquist — wavelengths ~6–16 px/cycle. At 16–64 px/cycle the field is so smooth that even the banned bilinear interpolator reads it within ~0.3% spectral-centroid error, so the D1 oracle cannot distinguish bicubic from bilinear and would silently pass a regression. Pair the fixture with an analytic-reference oracle: rebuild the exact plane-wave field from the manifest params (`fixtures/prng.ts`) and compare the rendered centroid against the true continuous field, so content variance cancels and only resampler error remains.

entry.evidence: app/ MapLibre map stayed blank with styleLoaded=false until the shim, after which the Teton hillshade + frame overlay rendered; probe returned rafCalls=0 vs intervalCalls=8 with visibilityState 'hidden'. AMENDED 2026-07-13: `computer{screenshot}` capture transiently un-hides the page, so across a session with cached tiles MapLibre CAN boot and appear fully rendered in screenshots with no shim — while an idle probe in the same session still measures visibilityState 'hidden' and 0 rAF/sec. So: screenshots of a booted map no longer imply the shim was used; the shim (or a real browser) is still needed for anything requiring *continuous* rAF (animations, first-boot without prior captures, read_page).
entry.falsifier: an idle (no recent screenshot) preview page measures nonzero rAF/sec, or a cold first load renders the map with no capture and no shim.
entry.lesson: The agent Browser/preview pane composites pages with document.visibilityState==='hidden', which fully freezes requestAnimationFrame (measured 0 rAF calls/sec) while timers keep running (setInterval fires normally). rAF-driven libraries — MapLibre GL above all — never boot: the canvas mounts and WebGL2 is available, but the style never loads ('load' never fires, isStyleLoaded stays false, console warns "There is no style added to the map"). Non-rAF code (React render, fetch, one-shot canvas draws in useEffect) works fine, so the browser render core + oscilloscope verify normally; WebAudio also runs (context resumes on a synthesized click, graph builds and plays). To screenshot an rAF-driven UI here, temporarily shim `window.requestAnimationFrame = cb => setTimeout(() => cb(performance.now()), 16)` (guard on import.meta.env.DEV && visibilityState==='hidden') and remove before commit; or verify in a real browser. Also on the hidden page read_page/find return empty (a11y viewport 0x0), so drive the UI via screenshot-coordinate clicks (the screenshot is 2× — click in the reported 800×450 space) and inspect app state with javascript_tool (e.g. a temporary window handle).

entry.evidence: app/src/lens.ts slope lens; the scope went from flat+spike to rich jagged detail after removing the seam wrap; measured centroid honest 44 (seam-free) vs seam-inflated 74, both vs elevation 11, on a 6 km Teton z12 frame.
entry.falsifier: differentiating a raw-wrap frame with `(i+1)%n` yields a musically detailed waveform (no dominant seam spike) at typical terrain.
entry.lesson: A slope (or any derivative/high-pass) "lens" on a wavetable frame reveals the fine landform detail that raw elevation buries in the first few harmonics — but it must NOT differentiate across the cycle's loop point in `raw` wrap mode. The seam is a large elevation jump (D4's legitimate buzz); differencing across it (`s[(i+1)%n]-s[i]`) makes one dominant spike that peak-normalization then amplifies to full scale, so every real terrain gradient shrinks to near-zero and the waveform reads as a flat line with a single click. Use a forward difference without wrapping (endpoints repeat their neighbor) so the seam contributes ~0 and the terrain gradient fills the waveform. Same caution applies to any future curvature/2nd-derivative lens.

entry.lesson: To keep audition audio continuous while the frame re-renders (rotation/shear/zoom/lens each re-read the terrain and produce a new table many times/sec), the voice must keep ALL synthesis state — read phase, morph, pitch, gain — inside ONE persistent AudioWorklet node and swap only the table buffer via `postMessage` (transfer the ArrayBuffer). The next audio sample then reads the new terrain at the same phase → zero-gap. The prior BufferSource-per-frame design forced a full teardown/rebuild of N looping sources on every `setTable`, so the voice audibly re-voiced "on settle" and could freeze mid-drag; no amount of debouncing fixes that, it just hides it. Corollary: once swaps are gap-free, drop the setTable debounce entirely — post the new table immediately for maximum liveness. Do control-rate smoothing (one-pole ~10 ms) on morph/gain inside the processor so swaps and scrubs stay click-free.

entry.evidence: 2026-07-14 added `terrain: TerrainStats` to RenderOutput (src/core/render.ts); `npx tsc --noEmit` clean and `vite build` ✓, while `tsc -p app --noEmit` reported TS2741 (missing `terrain` in app/src/terrain.ts renderPath) plus TS2345 in app/src/download.ts.
entry.falsifier: root `tsc --noEmit` reports an error introduced anywhere under `app/src/`.
entry.lesson: Two independent gaps compound into total blindness on `app/`. (1) The root `tsconfig.json` has `"include": ["src", "test"]` — `npx tsc --noEmit` from the root silently checks the CORE ONLY and exits 0 no matter what `app/` contains; the app has its own `app/tsconfig.json` that must be run as `tsc -p app --noEmit`. (2) `vite build` transpiles with **esbuild, which strips types without checking them** — a green build says nothing about types. So the habitual "tsc --noEmit && vite build → both green" proves the app compiles-as-JS and nothing more. Found by adding a required field to a core interface: the app constructed that interface without the field and *both* commands stayed green; a second, unrelated pre-existing type error (an invalid `BlobPart`) had been sitting in shipped export code undetected. Fix: `npm run typecheck` = `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p app --noEmit`; run THAT, never bare tsc. Related: this also explains why L0008's broken template literal escaped tsc — it lived in `app/`.

entry.evidence: raw terrarium tiles at 36.0,−122.5 — z6 min −4910/max 3931/uniq 5000; z8 −4007…−1121/uniq 5000; z10 −3551…−1630/uniq 5000; z11/z12/z13 min 0/max 0/**uniq 1**. Coastal Big Sur z12 reads 10.1% exact zeros (the ocean half is the hole). AwsTerrainSource throws on HTTP failure, so these zeros are a served fill, not a fetch error. Resolution maths computed at 36°N; GEBCO 15 arc-sec ≈ 450 m at the equator and the ~25 %-mapped / ~80 %-gravity-interpolated figures per GEBCO/Seabed 2030 (gebco.net, seabed2030.gebco.net, Scripps). Also measured: Esri RGB imagery detects *clear* water emphatically (deep Pacific/Tahoe/Michigan 99–100 % blue-dominant) with no false positives (Teton shadow 4.5 %, ice/desert/forest ~0 %), but misses turbid water entirely (Mississippi delta 0 %, Lake Erie 0 %, Amazon river 0.9 %) — RGB has no near-infrared, the band water actually absorbs, so no colour rule fixes that.
entry.falsifier: an open-ocean terrarium tile at z11+ returns varied nonzero elevations, or a z8 ocean tile returns a uniform value, or a global bathymetry grid finer than ~15 arc-sec appears.
entry.lesson: In the AWS/Tilezen terrarium DEM, open ocean carries **genuine bathymetry** — the deep Pacific reads −4910…−1121 m with thousands of unique values — but only up to about **z10**. From **z11 up, ocean tiles are a uniform all-zeros fill** (`uniq = 1`): not flat water, just *no data*. This matters three ways. (1) **Detection:** the exact water signal is `elevation < 0` (submerged), not flatness. Lakes are a separate case — genuinely flat-filled at their surface (Lake Michigan 176.9 m with 8 unique values; Tahoe 1897.5 m with 6). (2) **Synthesis:** reading open ocean at the app's default z12 yields a DC constant → silence. That's a data gap to surface honestly, not a timbre. (3) **Terrain-derived FX/stats mislead by zoom:** the same coordinate is ~600 m "roughness" at z8 and 0 at z12, so any terrain-type classifier must state the zoom it was measured at. General rule: before concluding anything from a uniform reading, **probe a second zoom** — data coverage varies by zoom independently of what's on the ground. **The z10 ceiling is physical — don't go looking for a better source.** At 36°N terrarium serves 124 m/px at z10, while the best *global* bathymetry grids (GEBCO 2023, SRTM15+, ETOPO 2022) are all 15 arc-sec ≈ 375 m native there — terrarium already oversamples its source ~3× at the ceiling, so z12 (31 m/px) would be 12× interpolation with zero new information. Worse, the grid overstates the truth: only ~25 % of the seafloor is mapped by modern multibeam, and ~80 % of the *deep* ocean is interpolated from satellite-gravity altimetry, which resolves seamounts and trenches but not fine detail. So there is no higher-resolution global bathymetry to swap in — the ocean is genuinely where the map runs out of information. Higher-res bathymetry exists only *regionally* (NOAA Coastal Relief Model 3 arc-sec ≈ 75 m for US coasts — worth ~1 extra zoom; EMODnet ~115 m for European seas; detailed NOAA grids for the Great Lakes), each a separate source/format — a real integration cost for one zoom level, nearshore only. Musical upshot: deep-ocean reads are legitimately smooth and low-harmonic, and that IS the data at its true resolution.

entry.evidence: 2026-07-14, added a comment containing \`max\` while documenting the saturation stage; `tsc`/`vite build` had last run BEFORE the edit, and the Node drive harness ran AFTER and passed (THD 2.1%→33.2%) — total green. The app rendered nothing: a Vite error overlay read "voice.ts:90:8 Expected ";" but found "max"". Only opening the preview surfaced it.
entry.falsifier: a backtick inside the PROCESSOR_SRC body compiles fine, or the regex-based harness fails on it.
entry.lesson: The AudioWorklet processor is authored as a JS string inside a **template literal** (L0005), so a single backtick anywhere in it — including in a prose comment, e.g. writing the route's \`max\` control markdown-style — silently terminates the string and breaks the file. The dangerous part is the verification gap: the Node DSP harness extracts the source with `/const PROCESSOR_SRC = \`([\s\S]*?)\`;/`, which matches on a backtick followed by `;`. A stray backtick mid-comment isn't followed by `;`, so the regex still finds the true terminator, the harness extracts the full body, and **the DSP tests keep passing on a file that no longer compiles**. Editing a comment is also exactly when you skip re-running tsc. Rules: no backticks in PROCESSOR_SRC (use "quotes"); after ANY edit inside it — comments included — re-run `tsc`, and drive the actual app, since only those catch it. A cheap guard: assert zero backticks in the extracted body.

entry.evidence: Place weather-region view (app/src/weatherGrid.ts). Live Open-Meteo probe over the Tetons: wide 0.6°×0.8° 8×8 lattice → 64 samples/64 distinct cells, inferred pitch 0.0001° lat (nonsense); tight 0.02°×0.02° → 64 samples/4 cells, pitch 0.0039°×0.0107°. Grid is ~1 km, not the ~0.1° assumed. Pivoted to lattice-tile rendering; default Teton view resolves 100 samples → 13 cells with visible blocks.
entry.falsifier: unique snapped coords from a coarse multi-point request fall on a regular lat/lon lattice (constant pitch in both axes) across a wide area.
entry.lesson: A point API that answers with *snapped* coordinates (Open-Meteo: ask lat 43.7412, get 43.7264) looks like an invitation to recover the model's cells — de-dupe the snapped coords, infer the pitch from their spacing, draw rectangles. Do not. Numerical-weather models commonly live on **projected** grids (HRRR/Lambert conformal, ICON/icosahedral), so their cell centres are *irregular* in lat/lon: spacing varies with position and the centres don't lie on an axis-aligned lattice at all. The min-gap pitch heuristic then returns garbage, and any rectangle drawn from it is invented geometry presented as measurement. Two tells that the premise is broken: (a) a lattice coarser than the grid yields as many "cells" as samples (nothing de-dupes), and (b) the inferred pitch is absurd — a 0.0001° gap can't exist on a grid whose pitch is supposedly ~0.004°. Instead render the **sampled field at your own lattice resolution** (one flat tile per sample): same-cell neighbours share a value, so real regions emerge visually with hard edges, and the picture claims only what was measured. Report `samples → distinct cells` as the resolution signal (equal ⇒ grid finer than the view).

entry.evidence: Place map rain overlay showed "Zoom Level Not Supported" at z12 (app/src/MapLayers.tsx); probe hashed RainViewer tiles z3–z12 for the Teton area vs the z12 placeholder → real to z7, placeholder z8+; setting source `maxzoom: 7` removed the placeholder (overzoomed z7 instead), verified in preview.
entry.falsifier: a MapLibre raster overlay with source maxzoom set to the provider's real max still shows provider placeholder tiles when the map zooms past it.
entry.lesson: A coarse raster tile overlay (weather radar, etc.) added to MapLibre without a `maxzoom` on its source will, above the provider's supported zoom, request tiles the provider doesn't have — and some providers return a **visible placeholder image** ("Zoom Level Not Supported" text baked into the PNG) rather than a 404 or a transparent tile, so it looks like a broken render, not a missing tile. Fix: set the raster source's `maxzoom` to the provider's true max, so MapLibre stops requesting higher-zoom tiles and instead **overzooms** (stretches) the deepest real tile. Find the real max empirically by hashing tiles: fetch the known-placeholder tile (a zoom you can see is broken) and compare each zoom's tile hash to it — the placeholder is byte-identical everywhere, and (crucially) is DISTINCT from an empty/transparent "no data here" tile, which is also identical-across-x but a different, smaller image. For RainViewer radar the real cap is **z7** (z8+ = placeholder), and 512-px tiles don't extend it.

entry.falsifier: a blob-URL worklet fails to load in Vite build or the preview pane while an `import.meta.url` asset URL succeeds there.
entry.lesson: Load an AudioWorklet processor by embedding its source as a string, making a `URL.createObjectURL(new Blob([src], {type:'application/javascript'}))`, and passing that to `audioWorklet.addModule()` (revoke after). This sidesteps bundler asset-URL handling (`new URL('./proc.js', import.meta.url)`, `?worker`, module-type quirks) that varies across Vite dev vs build and can silently fail to emit or serve the worklet file. The processor must be self-contained (no imports — worklet global scope has no module resolution), which the blob approach enforces by construction. Verified to work identically in Vite dev, production build, and the agent preview pane (which runs pages hidden — WebAudio + worklets still run there even though rAF is frozen, per L0002).

entry.lesson: functional_tension pulls the internal tension scalar toward per-degree targets (V=0.85, vii°=0.90, I=0). Measured across seeds 3/7/11: toggling it changed NEITHER the chord sequence NOR the fired-rule sequence — because no rule in the built-in ruleset gates on the tension value it moves. So it was completely inaudible (Julian: "really struggle to see any difference"). A feature that only writes a state field, with nothing downstream reading that field differently, is a no-op no matter how correct the field's values are. When adding a signal, confirm a consumer's BEHAVIOUR changes (diff the fired-rule trace), not just that the signal's value changed.

entry.evidence: 2026-07-08 session — search_voicings([0,2,4,7,11],root=0,{register:[48,84]}) with no from_voicing returned midi (59,60,62,64,67); gap-17 adoption seeds bar1 derived, then 25/26 bars engine-voiced in-register (commit fcd4b2b).
entry.falsifier: a from_voicing-less search_voicings call that returns an open (non-clustered) top match for a 5+ note chord by default, or an engine ranking option that prefers spread without an anchor.
entry.lesson: mts.search.search_voicings ranks by voice-leading distance ONLY when given from_voicing; with no from_voicing (the first bar) it ranks by compactness, so matches[0] for a 5–6 note chord (9ths/11ths) is a tight semitone cluster (e.g. Cmaj9 -> 59,60,62,64,67). Taking matches[0] uniformly makes the whole piece cluster, because every later bar voice-leads smoothly FROM that clustered start. Fix: realize the opening voicing with the local open-stack derived voicer, then use search_voicings(from_voicing=prev) from bar 2 on — open tessitura + smooth motion. Also: a too-tight max_voice_leading yields zero matches for some chord pairs; relax it once before falling back.

entry.lesson: Tonality response-4 recommended window_beats=8.0/hop_beats=2.0 as the shared structural-key geometry so Wend and Audiology read a file identically. Adopting it as validate_run's default MEASURABLY broke Wend's own key validation: seed 7 went from areas 3/4 matched (at 4.0/1.0) to 0/4 (at 8.0/2.0), because Wend's key areas are SHORT and the wide window dilutes them into one sharp home. A pinned cross-tool param is calibrated to the OTHER consumer's material grain (the alignment note assumes return-home pieces; Wend wanders in short areas) — adopting it wholesale can degrade your own reading. entry.evidence: 2026-07-08 — chord_legibility() seed 7; mismatches were all Am7→C6 / A11→Cmaj13 (pc-identical), content_legibility stayed 84% while root fell to 69% (commit e47c440).
entry.falsifier: a run where content and root legibility diverge but the content-only misses are genuinely foreign chords (not pc-rotations/subsets of the declared chord).
entry.lesson: A single "does the rendered chord match the declared chord" metric via segment_to_chords conflates two failures. Strict root-pc match penalizes chords that are pc-rotations of each other (Am7 = C6, Em7 = G6): the segmenter picks the pc-weight-dominant root, which needn't be Wend's declared root, and neither the key context nor the bass reliably flips it. Report BOTH: root legibility (is the intended centre/root recoverable) and content legibility (inferred salient pcs ⊆ declared voicing pcs — is a chord built from my pitches). The gap = benign root-ambiguity; only a content miss is truly foreign. Measured: rich 9ths root 69% / content 84%, 0 truly-foreign — rich chords read ambiguous, not wrong. Implication for the hybrid: root assertion is the bass's job, not the voicing's.

entry.falsifier: a Wend structural-key reading whose area matches materially improve with key_inertia on, or a local-track consumer where inertia does NOT reduce region count.
entry.lesson: Tonality's key_inertia (Viterbi switch-penalty continuity prior, versioned key-inertia.1) stops the key reading from flip-flopping when notes fit both keys — what Audiology runs on generated corpora. Where it helps depends on GRAIN: at the structural grain (reduce_to_structural_keys) it's a near no-op on Wend's output, because structural reduction already absorbs short blips (measured: identical area counts inertia off/on across 6 seeds). At the LOCAL grain (track_keys regions, before reduction) it cuts spurious key-flips ~34% (166→108 regions across 6 seeds). So adopt it where a consumer reads the RAW local track live — the Phase-J hybrid's tonicization-vs-modulation arbiter — not for structural validation. Separately: Wend's "everything heard sharp / areas 0/4" is UNDER-ASSERTION (surface doesn't ground its tonic), which inertia does NOT fix — don't reach for a continuity prior to cure a grounding problem. Per key-grain-alignment.md, pinning inertia on for a generated corpus must be declared in the channel so Audiology matches.

entry.evidence: 2026-07-08 — infer_key seed 11 A minor→C major (unrestricted) vs unchanged (restricted); seeds 7/42 stay D major at anchor 1.0 every-downbeat; legibility 94→84% unrestricted, 94% restricted.
entry.falsifier: a bass-only device that shifts structural_keys/infer_key toward the intended tonic on a genuinely sharp-drifting walk without a legibility cost.
entry.lesson: Under-assertion (Wend's declared key reads sharp — intended C heard as D) is NOT fixable from the bass. Tested a bass_anchor lever that plants the key tonic in the bass at structural beats (hyperdownbeats/cadences). MEASURED: (a) structural areas-matched and sharp-miss offsets DON'T move (one bass voice can't outweigh the chords+topline; and structural reduction smooths it); (b) it only flips the RELATIVE-ambiguity case (seed 11 A minor→C major, because C got pedaled under non-tonic chords) — and that flip costs 10pp of chord legibility (94→84%) precisely BECAUSE of those clashing pedals; (c) genuine sharp drift (seeds 7/42 read D) never flips even at max tonic weight — the CHORDS established D. Restricting the pedal to bars where the tonic is already a chord tone removes the legibility cost but also removes ALL grounding effect. So grounding power and legibility cost are the same knob — you can't get one without the other from the bass. Reverted. The real lever is HARMONIC: the walk must spend time on / cadentially return to tonic-function chords (assert the centre in the harmony, where key induction actually weighs it). Before building any "assert the key" feature, MEASURE whether it moves infer_key/structural_keys — an added voice that doesn't shift the pc-weight centroid is inert (cf. L0002).

entry.evidence: 2026-07-08 — engine-injected cadential_return, bar agreement 58/192→94/191 (commit 37c9b22); byte-identical at 0.
entry.falsifier: a walk where periodic tonic returns do NOT raise bar-level declared-vs-heard agreement, or where area-count proves a cleaner A/B for a harmony lever than bar-level agreement.
entry.lesson: The fix for "declared key doesn't READ as itself" (all inference drifts sharp) is to make the HARMONY assert its centre — land on the tonic (authentic cadence) at phrase heads — not to add a grounding voice (the bass failed, L0007). cadential_return (0..1) injects a tonic return at each hypermetric downbeat with that probability. MEASURED on the confound-free metric (bar-level track_keys-vs-declared agreement, which unlike area-count doesn't shift when the walk changes): 30%→49% across 6 seeds at 0.7, every seed ≥ baseline (seed 3: 6%→51%), journey preserved. Root cause it fixes: the builtin affirm_new_key rule fires only `when modulations >= 1`, so the INITIAL key is never cadentially affirmed and reads sharp from the start. GENERAL PRINCIPLE for this project: measure key-legibility with BAR-LEVEL local agreement (track_keys vs declared per bar), not area-count matched — area count changes when a harmony lever changes the walk, so it can't A/B a harmony change; bar-level agreement can.

entry.falsifier: a generation-time use of structural_keys that gates a chord choice before it's played (would need inference over unrealized output), or an arbiter classification that contradicts Tonality's own tonicization-absorption.
entry.lesson: In a GENERATOR, "structural_keys rules tonicization-vs-modulation" can't gate generation (structural_keys reads the OUTPUT, which doesn't exist until after the chord is chosen) — it's a post-generation VALIDATOR. arbitrate_keys() (validate.py) classifies each DECLARED key: modulation (a structural_keys area covers it), tonicization (only the local track_keys+key_inertia hears it, structurally absorbed), or not_heard (surface under-asserts). This is the shippable half of Phase J's "master declares, Tonality validates" design — buildable now WITHOUT the byte-breaking silent-master rearchitecture (which has load-bearing design questions still needing Julian). The arbiter also demonstrates the two key-legibility levers composing: cadential_return asserts the centre -> the arbiter reclassifies a declared key from not_heard/tonicization to a legible modulation (seed 3: 0->3 modulations as cr 0->0.7). Use key_inertia=True for the arbiter's LOCAL track (L0006) and bar-level agreement for its legibility number (L0008).

entry.evidence: 2026-07-08 — spread-aware _moves() reclassified functional_tension from "real lever" to "inert — internal only" (moves only tension_std), matching L0002; commit 64cf7f5.
entry.falsifier: a knob whose mean-swing exceeds the seed band on an output metric yet is verified inaudible/inert by other means (would mean the noise floor is the wrong gate).
entry.lesson: The L.1 knob-characterization harness flags a knob "inert" when its effect curves are flat. First cut called flat = mean-swing < 6% of the metric's observed range. That FALSE-POSITIVED functional_tension as a "real lever": its 2-point bool sweep showed key-legibility drifting 0.18→0.25, but that shift was smaller than the seed-to-seed spread — noise, not signal. Fix: a metric "moves" only if the mean swing beats BOTH 6% of range AND ~0.75× the median per-value seed spread (min-max band). Any characterization/guard that compares means across a swept parameter MUST compare the between-value signal to the within-value (seed) noise, or it will call noise an effect — worse than no guard, because it looks authoritative. Especially acute for few-point sweeps (bools) and high-variance metrics.

entry.evidence: goldens generated on node 24/darwin diverged on node 22/linux CI purely from Math.exp; fixed by `math.ts` (commit "Make core math platform-deterministic; regenerate goldens"); `packages/core/test/math.test.ts` asserts ≤1 ulp agreement with the builtins over 100k sampled points and pins edge cases.
entry.falsifier: if `math.test.ts` ever shows >1 ulp divergence the port is wrong; if a future Node/V8 guarantees correctly-rounded Math.exp/log (or goldens are regenerated per-platform), the custom impls become unnecessary.
entry.lesson: The byte-exact golden-chronicle contract requires core to use the fdlibm-derived `exp`/`log` in `packages/core/src/math.ts` for every simulation/harmony calculation — NOT `Math.exp`/`Math.log`. ECMA-262 leaves those two implementation-approximated, and V8 versions differ by ~1 ulp on rare inputs; a single differing ulp flips one Glauber/softmax sample and diverges the whole chronicle, but ONLY on the platform whose libm differs — so it passes locally and fails in CI (or vice versa). The fdlibm ports use only exactly-rounded IEEE-754 arithmetic, so they are bit-identical on every platform.

entry.evidence: a /tmp probe creating an easymidi Output surfaced in getInputs() only under dangerouslyDisableSandbox; the backgrounded `npm run live` launched with the flag and Live received it — human confirmed "plays as expected" (2026-07-09).
entry.falsifier: if a future harness grants CoreMIDI access to the sandbox by default, the flag is unnecessary; if the port becomes visible to another app without the flag, this is wrong.
entry.lesson: Launching the live MIDI CLI (or any easymidi/node-midi virtual-port creation) from the Claude Code Bash tool must pass `dangerouslyDisableSandbox: true`. Creating a CoreMIDI virtual source is a system-level op that hits the sandbox overlay: the node process reports success and the port "exists," but it is INVISIBLE to Ableton and other apps — a silent failure. Only with the sandbox disabled does the port appear in `easymidi.getInputs()` (next to "IAC Driver Bus 1") and become routable in Live. This is the MIDI instance of the machine's general gotcha (global CLAUDE.md: codesign/auval/~Library ops hit an overlay, not the real system).

entry.lesson: The single coherence scalar saturates to threshold in ~0.5 s (first ~9% of an epoch), crushing the musical arc — but adding a "more gradual" order parameter does NOT fix it. entry.evidence: live verification into Ableton 2026-07-13 — Start-only follower on a playing set read "stopped 120 BPM pulse 0"; after the fix it locked on connect (RUNNING, pulse advancing 8/sec at 120) and tracked a live 120→100 change in ~2s; span estimate cut jitter ±20→±1. `packages/midi/test/clock-follow.test.ts` covers the mid-playback case.
entry.falsifier: a DAW set to "send clock always (even when stopped)" would read as running while stopped under rule (1); if that must be supported, gate `running` on a clock-presence timeout plus explicit Stop instead.
entry.lesson: Two non-obvious traps when following a DAW's MIDI clock. (1) A follower that sets `running` only on a Start (0xFA) silently fails to lock when it connects to an ALREADY-playing DAW: the DAW streams clock (0xF8) but sends no fresh Start, so the follower estimates tempo yet reports stopped / position frozen at 0. Fix: treat clock arrival itself as transport-running + position-advancing (Live and most DAWs emit clock only while playing); Start realigns the downbeat (count→0), Stop halts, Song-Position jumps. (2) Estimate tempo from the time SPAN over a window of clocks (~2 quarters: `bpm = 2.5*(n-1)/span`), NOT by averaging per-tick intervals — MIDI/IAC jitter and Node event-loop batching make single intervals noisy (±20 BPM observed), which wobbles the `pulseToSeconds` note due-times; span-based gives ±1%.

entry.evidence: Written into EDGEWISE DECISIONS #4 as "a voice must accept live width/position updates after note-on"; implementing the JUCE shell against CATENA's (which had already settled the opposite, its DECISIONS #6/#9) showed that requirement to be physically incoherent. entry.falsifier: A continuous-excitation instrument (bowing, blowing) where the excitation genuinely persists — there the strike/pickup split does not apply and width/position ARE continuous state. EDGEWISE is strike-only (brief §6), so this holds here.
entry.lesson: For struck instruments, mallet width and strike position are properties of an EVENT: they enter once at note-on and are baked into the partial amplitudes. Nothing can re-shape a strike already ringing — the chain was struck at a place, with a mallet of a size. So MPE pressure/timbre select the next strike on that channel, and this costs no expressivity in practice because MPE controllers send pressure and slide BEFORE the note-on. When a genuinely continuous post-strike gesture is wanted, the honest mechanisms are a pickup (re-tapping already-solved mode shapes at a moving position) or damping — not retroactively re-striking. Design the voice around the event/continuous split before writing it; retrofitting the distinction means rewriting the voice.

entry.falsifier: The port deliberately diverges (e.g. a banded solver replacing Jacobi for speed) — then fixtures no longer define correctness and the new implementation needs its own analytic anchoring instead.
entry.lesson: When porting a verified core to a second language, export JSON fixtures from the reference and assert the port against them (1e-9 relative; the algorithms are identical, so only libm's last ulp differs). Two independent implementations agreeing is a far stronger oracle than either alone. Two non-obvious requirements: (1) mirror the reference EXACTLY — same sweep counts, same thresholds, same RNG draw order, and `std::stable_sort` to match JS's stable `Array.sort` (degenerate eigenvalues, like the two edge modes, tie and would otherwise order differently); (2) CI must regenerate the fixtures and fail on any diff, or a physics change silently leaves the port verified against yesterday's truth — a green build that proves nothing.

Then the replacement hook's first version returned exit 0 on all 15 must-block cases because of the missing `--`; found only by writing `.claude/hooks/tests/push-guard.test.sh` and running it. Now wired into `./verify fast` as `hook_gate` — reintroducing the missing `--` makes verify exit 1 with the failing cases printed, restoring it returns 0. entry.falsifier: Claude Code changes Bash permission matching from prefix to full-pattern/glob semantics, which would make the settings.json half of this obsolete (check the current permissions docs before relying on it). The grep half is falsified only by a POSIX behaviour change and is unlikely to rot. Also falsified in spirit if a project's gates are all content-based rather than flag-based, where prefix matching is adequate.
entry.lesson: Two independent failure modes hit the same guard within an hour, and neither was visible by reading. (1) **settings.json Bash deny rules are PREFIX matches.** `Bash(git push --delete*)` does not match `git push origin --delete x` — the spelling anyone actually types — and a broader allow rule like `Bash(git push origin *)` then matches it instead. Deny-by-prefix cannot express "this flag anywhere in the command", so any rule about a FLAG belongs in a PreToolUse hook that greps the whole command string; settings.json is defense-in-depth, not the mechanism. The kit's own `pretool-deny.sh` shipped with the identical adjacent-flag hole (`git push --force` only). (2) **A shell guard whose regex begins with a dash silently allows everything**: `grep -qE "$PAT"` with `PAT='--force|…'` makes grep parse the pattern as an option, error on every call, and return non-match — so the guard passes 100% of input while looking correct and while its own comments claim safety. Fix: `grep -qE -- "$PAT"`. The general rule both instances teach: a safety gate is code with an inverted failure signature — when normal code breaks you see an error, when a gate breaks you see GREEN. So a gate is not done until it has been run against known-bad input and observed to reject it, and that run belongs in the blocking oracle, not in a one-off manual check. Corollary: expect the strict version to false-positive on prose (a commit message quoting the forbidden command trips it); fix that by passing bodies via `-F`/`--body-file`, never by teaching the guard to skip quoted text, which is a quoting bypass.

(2) **A shell guard whose regex begins with a dash silently allows everything**: `grep -qE "$PAT"` with `PAT='--force|…'` makes grep parse the pattern as an option, error on every call, and return non-match — so the guard passes 100% of input while looking correct and while its own comments claim safety. Fix: `grep -qE -- "$PAT"`. The general rule both instances teach: a safety gate is code with an inverted failure signature — when normal code breaks you see an error, when a gate breaks you see GREEN. So a gate is not done until it has been run against known-bad input and observed to reject it, and that run belongs in the blocking oracle, not in a one-off manual check. entry.evidence: 2026-07-30, this repo, both observed live in one turn: the Stop gate demanded re-verify of a clean tree twice after scratchpad PR-body writes; a web-research subagent with clean `git status` was told "edits exist that have not been verified". Fixed and negative-tested 2026-07-31 — reverting each hook to its pre-fix version makes `./verify fast` exit 1 failing EXACTLY the cases that describe its defect (4 out-of-repo cases; 4 subagent cases) and nothing else, with the lead-blocking cases identical before and after. Payload contract confirmed against real captured `SubagentStop` payloads, not just docs (`hook_event_name`, `agent_id`, `agent_type` all present as documented). Full account: DECISIONS R-011, traces/2026-07-31-hook-false-positives.md. Corollary caught in the act: the first version of the dirty-flag test ran the hook from the wrong cwd and reported the UNFIXED hook as passing the cases it fails — see [[L0002]], the test is not trustworthy until watched failing for the right reason.
entry.falsifier: a workflow where a subagent legitimately owns the verify-and-report duty (a dedicated "closer" role that runs `./verify` and writes the trace) would make the lead-only rule wrong for that role — re-scope rather than reuse. Also falsified if Claude Code makes hook payloads stop carrying `agent_id`, or scopes harness state per session itself. The scratchpad half is falsified if agent scratch space moves inside the repo, at which point path-based scoping stops separating the two.
entry.lesson: L0002's failure was a gate that could not fire; this is its mirror, and it is not the lesser bug. Both instances have one shape: **shared state whose scope does not match the scope of the event that reads it.** (1) A repo-global "dirty" flag was raised by ANY Edit/Write because the hook never read its stdin payload — including writes to the session scratchpad, which the previous fix (R-008: commit messages and PR bodies via files) had just guaranteed a steady stream of. The closing gate then demanded re-verification of a provably clean tree. (2) The same repo-global flag was wired to `SubagentStop`, so a read-only subagent — no writes anywhere in its transcript — was blocked over the LEAD's unverified edits and burned its final report answering the hook. Neither rule was wrong; both were scoped wrong. The generalisable moves: a per-tree flag is cashed out only by the session that owns the tree and the report (the lead), never by a subagent, which cannot discharge it — read-only roles are forbidden from clearing it and the report is not theirs to make; and a path-triggered hook must actually parse `tool_input.file_path` and compare `realpath` on BOTH sides (on macOS the scratchpad arrives as `/private/tmp/…` while `/tmp` symlinks to it, so a string compare misclassifies one spelling of the same directory). Nothing is lost by skipping subagents, because `PostToolUse` fires inside them too — an implementer's writes still raise the flag and the lead's own Stop catches them; assert that as a test case rather than trusting the argument. Direction of failure still decides the default: unclassifiable input counts as an edit (a false "dirty" costs one verify run; a false "clean" lets an unverified edit past). And the meta-move: `hook_gate` was widened from one hard-coded filename to a glob that is RED on zero tests found — both defects reached production while a hook-test gate already existed, because it only ran the one test someone remembered to name. **A false positive is a gate failure of the same severity as a false negative: a gate that fires at nothing gets routed around, and the routing-around is permanent while the noise is only annoying.**

entry.evidence: 2026-08-01/02, phase0b bench: the 0-landings shadowed-binding bug, the 11.75 dB phase-locking bug (rigid rotation vs single-phase, found via the identity case), the unstoppable renderSrc (measured 0.094→0 on three stop paths), the null at 0.00 cents vs the 215.3 Hz false confirmation, and the self-inflicted 'gain' crash. Traces: 2026-07-31-q003-stft.md, docs/phase0b-findings.md §6–§8.
entry.falsifier: a defect class where the observable is genuinely inaccessible (timing races, allocation behaviour, anything requiring instrumentation the product cannot carry) — there, mechanism inspection is the only tool and this lesson does not apply. Also weakened wherever the observable is expensive enough that measuring every hypothesis is impractical; then predict first and measure the discriminating case only.
entry.lesson: Across one build stretch, every real defect was caught by measuring an OUTPUT and every phantom by inspecting a mechanism. Concretely: a harness reported 0 landings from 72 launched rays and threw nothing (found by comparing landings against the LAUNCH positions rather than against themselves); an offline render lost 11.75 dB (localised instantly by rendering through the EMPTY bench, where nothing optical happens — through the prism, "the geometry throws energy away" was a completely plausible and wrong story); a stop control that did nothing was proved fixed by tapping the output and watching level go 0.094 → 0, not by reading the wiring. **The sharp corollary is about resolution.** A null test using an 11.7 Hz peak finder returned 215.3 Hz for a 220 Hz input — a number consistent with BOTH transparency and a 2% error, so worthless as evidence — and it happened to match a failure that had been predicted in advance (bin-rounding should quantise pitch), so it read as confirmation. Measuring properly (16384-point FFT + parabolic interpolation) gave 0.00 cents: the prediction was wrong and the comfortable reading was the incorrect one. So: state the expected failure BEFORE measuring, then check the instrument can actually resolve it; if the measurement cannot distinguish your hypothesis from its negation, it is not a result. And the counter-discipline — a crash reported as "Cannot read properties of null (reading 'gain')" was the TEST HARNESS, not the product: a diagnostic had assigned the AudioContext directly, so the app's init took its already-initialised branch and never built the nodes. Reporting it would have sent a human chasing nothing. Before reporting a defect found while instrumenting, re-run it on a clean state you did not touch.

entry.evidence: 2026-08-09, `harness/algorithms/baseline.py`. Bin-wise magnitude interpolation is specified in BRIEF.md as "expected to sound like a crossfade". The first implementation switched phase wholesale at t=0.5; measured on pair A it put source A's 220 Hz fundamental at −96 dB at the midpoint (magnitude present, but carrying B's frame-to-frame-incoherent phase, so 75%-overlap add cancelled it) and sat 0.642 normalised RMS from a literal 50/50 crossfade — i.e. it collapsed to pure B. Per-bin phase from the louder contributor gives 0.006. The defect made the control WORSE than the crossfade it was meant to embody.
entry.falsifier: A project where the control's defects are reliably caught by comparison against candidates rather than by direct verification — i.e. where a broken baseline shows up as anomalous candidate results rather than as uniformly flattering ones.
entry.lesson: A baseline exists to be a FAIR floor, so a bug in the control is more dangerous than the same bug in a candidate — it silently inflates every later comparison, and nothing downstream can detect it because the control is the reference. Verify that the control reproduces the behaviour it is supposed to model, as a measurement, BEFORE any candidate is compared to it. The trap is that a broken control still renders, still looks plausible on a spectrogram, and still produces every metric.

entry.evidence: 2026-08-09, checking whether the baseline visits the 275 Hz midpoint between a 220 Hz and a 330 Hz source. At the harness STFT's 23.4 Hz bins (2048 @ 48 kHz) the midpoint read 60.5 against flanking peaks of 28.7 and 135.5 — apparently substantial midpoint energy. A single windowed FFT over the whole 2 s render (0.50 Hz resolution) put the same point at −119.5 dB. The first number was Hann skirts from both neighbours; it was nearly reported as a finding.
entry.falsifier: A case where a between-partials measurement at coarse resolution agrees with the fine-resolution value — which would mean leakage was not dominating and the check is unnecessary.
entry.lesson: Probing a weak quantity in the frequency gap between two strong ones is the classic way to measure the analysis window instead of the audio. Before reading such a number as a finding, check that the resolution can actually resolve the gap (bin spacing = sr/window) and re-measure with a window long enough that the partials of interest fall on distinct bins. The tell is a "midpoint" value that is implausibly HIGH relative to the peaks flanking it.

entry.evidence: This spin-up, 2026-08-08 — the session's own `settings.local.json` had already created `.claude/`, so the harness copy landed at `.claude/.claude/settings.json`; caught only because the follow-up `chmod +x .claude/hooks/*.sh` failed with "no matches found". entry.falsifier: A `cp -R a/.claude b/.claude` into a pre-existing `b/.claude` that produces a merged tree rather than a nested one (would mean the behaviour is platform- or cp-version-specific rather than general POSIX semantics).
entry.lesson: `cp -R <kit>/.claude <project>/.claude` does NOT merge — if the destination `.claude/` already exists (Claude Code creates one for `settings.local.json` the moment a session opens in the folder), cp places the source *inside* it as `.claude/.claude/`. Nothing errors and the scaffold looks complete, but `settings.json` and `hooks/` are one level too deep, so every hook path in the settings file resolves to nothing and the whole determinism layer is silently absent. Copy the *contents* (`cp -R <kit>/.claude/. <project>/.claude/`) whenever the destination may pre-exist, and confirm with `find .claude -type f` rather than `ls .claude`.

entry.evidence: measured margins on both profiles (C triad 0.073 vs 0.268; A minor 0.195 vs 0.039); Tonality `integrations/terrane/notice-cbms-default*.md`; TERRANE Tonality PR #88 ack.
entry.falsifier: `read_key()` returns a `profile_version` other than `kk-1982.1`, OR a future Tonality release adds a `profile_version` kwarg to the library `infer_key`.
entry.lesson: TERRANE consumes `infer_key`'s margin as a continuous control signal (clarity→ruggedness, home-pull gain), so the key profile MUST be pinned to `kk-1982.1` — the margin scale is what the feel is calibrated against. The library signature is `infer_key(material, *, profiles=None)`; there is NO `profile_version` kwarg (that selector exists only on the MCP *tools*). Pin with `infer_key(w, profiles=load_key_profiles("kk-1982.1"))` (see `terrane/tonality_client.py::pinned_profiles`). Passing `profile_version=` raises `TypeError` and silently falls through to Tonality's default, which flipped to `tkp-cbms.1` on 2026-06-17. CBMS is mode-asymmetric on margin (major inflates, minor collapses — A minor margin 0.195→0.039 via its relative-major bias), which the clarity mapping renders as spurious minor-key terrain instability. Rule of thumb: ranking-accuracy consumers want CBMS; margin-as-signal consumers (us) want KK.

entry.falsifier: a build where parity still holds with -ffp-contract=on or with an exact integer LCG — that would mean the rounding never actually bites. TESTED 2026-08-06: rebuilding with -ffp-contract=fast gave 89.22% max deviation and 40/72 cells failing, so the falsifier was exercised and the lesson survived — promoted to canonical on that basis.
entry.lesson: tools/verify.js's asperity generator is `seed=(seed*1103515245+12345)&0x7fffffff`. The product reaches ~2^61, past the 2^53 where doubles stop representing every integer, so V8 ROUNDS it — this is not an exact integer LCG. Porting it as a "proper" uint32/uint64 LCG changes every noise sample and silently breaks matrix parity; replaying the double rounding in C++ instead makes all 72 cells match the pinned golden to its printed precision. Two traps: the C++ core must compile with -ffp-contract=off (an FMA keeps the full-width product and diverges on the FIRST call), and the RNG must be drawn unconditionally per sample even when roughness is 0, or the noise stream desynchronises.

entry.lesson: JUCE regenerates Contents/Resources/moduleinfo.json AFTER its own ad-hoc signing step, breaking the seal. A broken-seal bundle is skipped by DAW scanners with no error and no host-log entry — it simply never appears, which reads as a code bug and sends you debugging the wrong layer. entry.evidence: DECISIONS.md D011; `c++ -ffp-contract=fast` build vs node tools/parity.mjs; contrast with sibling Catena, whose closed-form eigensolver tolerates 1e-9 on ubuntu — chaos, not language, is what forces the platform pin.
entry.falsifier: a parity run on a different libm/platform that lands within a few percent rather than either exact or wildly off — that would mean the amplification is bounded and a portable tolerance exists.
entry.lesson: a 110k-sample nonlinear stick-slip integration amplifies last-ulp floating-point differences into macroscopic ones. Measured: -ffp-contract=fast (last-ulp class perturbation) moves matrix cells by up to 89.22% and fails 40/72 against a golden the correct build matches at 0.00%. Consequences: (1) tightening a parity tolerance is pointless — there is no "slightly drifted" regime between bit-identical and wildly wrong, so ±20% and ±5% detect exactly the same faults; (2) the parity gate is only meaningful on the platform the golden came from, so CI runs macos-latest, not ubuntu (a different libm perturbs tanh/exp/sqrt the same way); (3) add a libm-free determinism check (the RNG) so an arithmetic regression is localised instead of surfacing as an uninformative whole-matrix failure.

entry.evidence: TRIBOS tanh(Σ·0.8) mix, 7-voice ROSIN chord: 2.42% of samples pinned >0.98 and RMS rising 0.35→0.57 with polyphony; after ÷√n + soft-knee compressor, 0.00% pinned, peak 0.88, RMS flat ~0.25. DECISIONS D013, docs/PHYSICS.md §6a.
entry.falsifier: a voice architecture where the per-voice saturator is the intended sound and summing headroom is reserved upstream — there the wall is deliberate.
entry.lesson: when each voice ends in its own saturator, the per-voice output is bounded but the SUM is not — n voices reach n, and a fixed mix gain then drives the master stage into a wall. The tell is a user reporting "sounds like an amplifier" that playing quietly does not fix: the input level is not what is clipping, the voice COUNT is. Measure pinned-sample percentage against voice count rather than trusting a single-note render, and normalise by voice count (÷√n, smoothed — stepping it on note-on/retire is itself a click) before any master gain.

entry.evidence: src/dsp/tribos/voice.hpp beginSteal/retrigger; regression "voice-steal declick" measures steal step 0.0043 vs sustain step 0.0067, and "retrigger keeps heat" confirms 42 C survives a retrigger that previously reset to 20 C ambient. DECISIONS D015.
entry.falsifier: an instrument where note-on genuinely should reinitialise everything (a pure one-shot sampler) — there the reset is correct and only the fade matters.
entry.lesson: zeroing a still-ringing voice's state on note-on is a step discontinuity — the click heard when retriggering a decaying note. Two fixes, and the second is the one that gets missed: (1) fade a genuinely stolen voice out over a few ms before reusing it; (2) route a SAME-note retrigger to a path that resets nothing, because the blanket reset also discards per-voice state that is supposed to persist — in TRIBOS the contact temperature, i.e. the instrument's entire premise. Test it with a relative oracle: max sample-to-sample step around the steal versus the max step during ordinary sustain, since a noisy signal has no meaningful absolute threshold.

entry.evidence: response §4 + response-2 (2026-07-08), Tonality agent of record — recipe answer, no engine work for v1; brief-2 (the K-session question) resolved by scope-separation.
entry.falsifier: a cross-scope joint model or a same-scope-repeat need triggers the clustered slice; or `induce_ruleset`'s piece = input-Sequence semantics change; or graded sample-weights (gap 20) reframes the piece unit.
entry.lesson: When building liked/disliked corpora for `induce_rules` / `compare_rulesets` / `build_transition_matrix`, pool all of a run's same-label spans into ONE pseudo-piece per run — `pieces = runs`. Multiple spans from the SAME run are NOT independent pieces; counting them separately inflates `induce_ruleset`'s piece-presence support + Fisher independence, the exact significance-corrupting trap as span duplication (a hard-constraint gotcha), one level up. The Wend worry — one `run_id` rated in K PARALLEL scoped sessions (D9/D10, same music, different scope+satisfaction) — DISSOLVES via scope-separation (response-2): because each scope is mined as its OWN corpus, the K sessions land in K *different* corpora, so any one corpus sees the run exactly once → within a corpus, `pieces = runs`. Unit is `(run, scope)`; whole-composition / unscoped ratings = one-piece-per-run in the global corpus. Residual needing a `run_id` grouping-key (clustered/mixed-effects) slice — deferred, wont named — ONLY for multiple SAME-scope sessions of one run, or a cross-scope joint model. COROLLARY (train/test): when scoring a distribution with `TransitionMatrix.cross_entropy(held_out)` — including the D11 recovery metric — split the held-out set BY RUN, never by span/session, or same-run material leaks across the split → optimistic perplexity. The run is the unit for partitioning too.

entry.falsifier: a cross-scope joint model (the deferred clustered slice) makes K sessions jointly informative for a single scope's significance.
entry.lesson: Wend's parallel scoped sessions (D9/D10 — one `run_id` rated under multiple scope-sets) are BOTH a per-part attribution mechanism AND a cross-scope render-efficiency lever: one audited run feeds K scope corpora at once, so a single listen harvests bass-signal AND topline-signal (determinism makes the render cheap, so this efficiency is real). They are NOT within-scope power multiplication — within any one scope, effective sample size = the distinct runs carrying that scope (+1 per run, never +K). So the D10 staging buffer earns its complexity for attribution + efficiency; for significance, lean on more DISTINCT runs per scope. Squares with D12 (scoped sessions = optional prior / accelerant, not the mechanism). Practical: don't over-invest in re-auditioning one run many ways to "get more data" for a scope — audit more distinct runs.

entry.evidence: FOUNDATIONS' CI carried the kit template's `paths-ignore: ["**/*.md","docs/**"]` while its oracle is almost entirely markdown/JSON consistency (INDEX↔LIBRARY, manifest survey answers, correspondent registry, contract version). Every green tick on a docs change had run nothing. Removing the filter (PR #1, 2026-08-10) turned CI red in 6s and exposed two gates broken the whole time: the correspondent sweep failed off the dev machine because it treated absent sibling repos as our data being wrong (a machine detector, not a check), and the standby-notice hash was computed, printed, and compared to no baseline while its own comment claimed it detected un-versioned edits. Both verified fixed against a HOME-redirected CI simulation before pushing (DECISIONS #28).
entry.falsifier: A project where path-filtered CI ran zero times on a whole class of change over many months and no defect reached the branch — or a case where observing a gate fail on purpose cost more than the defects it would have caught. Also falsified if the simulated-environment discipline turns out to produce false confidence, i.e. a simulation that passes where the real runner fails.
entry.lesson: Two failure modes hide behind the same green tick and both survive indefinitely because the signal for "ran and passed" is identical to the signal for "did not run" and to "ran a check that cannot fail". (a) A CI path filter that skips the job entirely — the badge is green, the coverage is zero, and nobody looks because nothing is red. (b) A check whose result is computed and then never compared to anything, which passes on every input including wrong ones. The countermeasure is not more checks but observing each gate FAIL once on purpose, and — for environment-sensitive checks — running the suite in a simulated foreign environment locally rather than discovering machine dependence through a push/wait/read cycle in public.
entry.recurred: 2026-08-10 — and the recurrence sharpened the lesson. A THIRD mode sits beside the two above and is worse than either: CI that runs, FAILS LOUDLY, and is never read. FOUNDATIONS' main was red for nine consecutive runs across two days (2026-08-08 21:03 → 2026-08-10) while the local oracle was green, and the agent asserted "CI passing" in a delivered artifact on the strength of one check made before the breakage. Not indistinguishable-from-passing — simply unobserved. The distinction matters for the countermeasure: filters and dead checks are fixed by testing gates, but an unread signal is fixed only by something that READS it. Concrete mitigation: `./verify ci` queries main's published conclusion (kept out of `fast`, which must stay offline), charter-bound to run at phase gates. Honest limit, recorded: this is reminder-grade, not enforcement — enforcement would mean a network call in the hot path, which is a worse trade. | recurred: 2026-08-10 (HYPERSAW, second origin, arrived from the opposite direction) — the general form is **the check and the thing checked shared an assumption**, and a fidelity oracle is its purest case: parity is structurally blind to any defect the reference and the port SHARE, and worse than blind, every passing scenario certifies it. HYPERSAW's consonance gravity integrated with dt=block length, so output depended on buffer SUBDIVISION; all 147 parity scenarios passed for the bug's entire life and *could not have failed*, because generator and checker used the same subdivision. Their fix then shipped the same defect smaller — a grid fixed in samples rather than time, settle time drifting +0.42% at 96 kHz — invisible to goldens generated at 44.1 kHz only. A ~40-line reference-free property check found both. Their taxonomy is the countermeasure and is the reusable part: FIDELITY oracles (parity, goldens) need a reference and do not survive changing it; INVARIANT oracles need none and do survive; a project needs both, and having only the first is the default state nobody notices. Our instances were gates that could not FAIL; theirs was an oracle that could not SEE. FOUNDATIONS' F2 gate gained acceptance criterion 1b as a result (DECISIONS #31).

entry.lesson: CI builds every tool target on windows-latest/MSVC, and each new add_executable repeats the same three traps: (1) no M_PI without _USE_MATH_DEFINES — use a local kPi constant (bit twice in one day: renderer_bench, then trajectory_check); (2) -O3 is not an MSVC flag — guard target_compile_options with if(NOT MSVC); (3) the project links the static MSVC runtime project-wide (CMAKE_MSVC_RUNTIME_LIBRARY at root — clap-wrapper only sets it in its own scope, and mixing /MT with /MD is an LNK2038 wall). entry.evidence: PR #4 stranding (traces/2026-07-18-gui-polish.md); PR #5/#6 miss; PR #38 stacked-base stranding → rescue cherry-pick (traces/2026-07-19-subosc-rescue-octave.md). And 2026-07-22: ~14 detune-lab commits pushed to PR #70's branch across ~10 turns AFTER #70 had merged — stranded off main until a fresh-branch rescue (PR #72). FOUR occurrences now; the failure is not knowing the rule but not RUNNING the pre-push state check (rule 0) — make it a reflex. FIFTH OCCURRENCE 2026-08-11, and the sharpest: PR #261 (base = an intermediate branch) is badged MERGED by GitHub, yet its content never reached main — the base had ALREADY been consumed by its own PR before the child landed on it, so the child merged into a dead branch and main had zero references to the fix. The audit that followed found the F2 conformance tools absent from main the same way. NEW RULE (4): A MERGED BADGE IS NOT EVIDENCE THE WORK IS IN MAIN. It reports that a PR closed against ITS OWN BASE, which may not be main. Verify by CONTENT — grep main for a distinctive identifier from the change, or `git merge-base --is-ancestor` — never by the badge, and never by the human's report of having merged it.
entry.falsifier: a repo setting (auto-merge with required approvals, or reliable stacked-PR retargeting) makes post-file pushes and stacks safe.
entry.lesson: Commits repeatedly miss their merge window: PR #4 merged into a stacked base after the base's own PR had merged (stranding the GUI off main); a layout+ADSR commit pushed to PR #5's branch landed minutes after the human merged it; and PR #38 (stacked with base=#37's branch) merged INTO that already-merged base — GitHub did NOT retarget the child to main after the base merged, so the sub-osc commit never reached main and needed a cherry-pick rescue. The human merges asynchronously and GitHub's stacked-PR retargeting is unreliable. Rules: (0) BEFORE pushing to any branch you did NOT create this turn, run `gh pr view <branch> --json state` and confirm it is OPEN — a merged PR's branch is frozen, and further pushes strand silently (this is the check that was skipped repeatedly); (1) once a PR is filed its branch is frozen — new work starts a NEW branch off main, even for "the same topic"; (2) prefer independent branches off main over stacked PRs; if you must stack, after the BASE merges immediately verify the child's PR retargeted to main AND that its commit is an ancestor of origin/main (git merge-base --is-ancestor / git branch -r --contains) before assuming it landed; (3) stacked PRs state their merge order in the body.

raw: [L0016] CALIBRATE THE DETECTOR BEFORE TRUSTING IT — run any new defect metric on a known-CLEAN and a known-BAD signal first; a metric that does not report ~zero on the clean case is measuring the signal, not the defect | canonical | added: 2026-07-28 | tags: parity-oracle, realtime-perf | lesson: THREE TIMES IN ONE SESSION I built a measurement instrument, got numbers that looked reasonable, and was measuring the wrong thing entirely. (1) An aliasing metric summed every non-harmonic FFT bin — it was accumulating Hann-window leakage from a dozen strong harmonics across thousands of bins, and reported a textbook-clean polyBLEP sawtooth at -27.7 dB instead of -149.5 dB. (2) A formant locator detrended the spectrum by +20log10(k) to cancel the saw's rolloff — that tilt over-weights the top octaves so hard it finds noise, and it reported 3190 Hz for an 800 Hz target. (3) A click detector thresholded |x[n]-x[n-1]| — on a 1200 Hz sine that is just the slope (~0.17/sample at 44.1 kHz), so it reported 2700 "jumps" in a perfectly clean signal, and I nearly chased a bug that did not exist. THE COMMON SHAPE: a threshold on the WRONG DERIVATIVE (or the wrong domain) measures the signal itself rather than the defect. WHY IT SURVIVES SCRUTINY: in all three cases the RANKING between configurations stayed roughly correct, so A/B comparisons still "worked" and nothing looked broken; only the absolute value was absurd. What saved me each time was noticing the absolute number was implausible against a reference I happened to know (a clean polyBLEP saw is ~-150 dB, not -27). That is luck, and it fails silently whenever I do NOT already know the right answer. THE RULE, which is cheap because both cases almost always already exist: before trusting a new detector, run it on (a) a signal known to be CLEAN — it MUST report ~zero, and if it does not, it is measuring the signal; and (b) a signal known to be DEFECTIVE — it MUST report large. Only then interpret real results. Corollary: plausible rankings are NOT validation. Domain-general — applies to any residue, noise floor, crosstalk, error rate, or A-minus-B metric where B is orders of magnitude larger than A. THE SPECTRAL CASE, absorbed here: when measuring a small quantity beside a large one, never define the small one as "total minus large" — find a place in the domain where the large quantity is structurally ABSENT and measure there. Summing every non-harmonic FFT bin measures Hann-window LEAKAGE from a dozen strong harmonics across thousands of bins, not aliasing; sampling at inter-harmonic midpoints ((k+0.5)*f0), where the nearest harmonic is hundreds of bins away, measures the residue. Applies to spectral residue, noise floors, crosstalk, and any A-minus-B metric where B is orders of magnitude bigger. | evidence: 2026-07-28 shape-lab session, all three instances measured and corrected: aliasing -27.7 -> -149.5 dB after inter-harmonic midpoint sampling (and it then revealed an 87 dB spread the broken metric had compressed to 15 dB, incl. the fractional-sync hot spot it hid entirely); formant locator replaced with a 1/3-octave envelope peak; click detector replaced with 2nd-difference outliers vs the robust local median, which then correctly read 0/s on integer sync and 300/s on ratio 4.37. | falsifier: a detector that passes the clean/defective calibration pair is later shown to be measuring the wrong quantity anyway — then calibration is insufficient and a stronger validation (e.g. an independently-derived reference implementation) is required. | supersedes: absorbs L0014 (the spectral case) — consolidated 2026-08-11
